The Nether here is &areal&r, with terrain and fortresses, and the End is real too. There's no ore in either: in the second season there's none in any world, and chests in structures hold no raw materials. Chemistry paves the way there: the obsidian for the portal is built from atoms, and there's no lava in the world. From here on, everything revolves around one loop. Dissolve the rock down to atoms. Build what you need out of the atoms. Discover that the element you need isn't in the rock. Get it from a reactor. It takes six chapters to run out of periodic table, and the seventh to extend it yourself: to make element &b119&r, which does not exist in nature.

“Compounds”, “Nether and End” and “Industrial Chemistry” are chemistry for real. “Annihilation” is its peak. “Settlement” is there so the world has something to look at. “Twilight Forest” is a separate world that opens as early as first power. “Challenges” are entirely optional: you go there for the sport, not for progress.

Fuel that costs more than what it smelts is a signpost, not a balance mistake. A coal furnace isn't industry, it's a campfire; real energy starts in the next chapter. Until then, burn only what you can't do without.

The scale was set by &6Alchemistry&r itself: its Dissolver breaks an iron ingot into exactly &b16&r atoms. So an ingot here isn't a lump of metal but a fixed-size portion of matter, and from now on everything in the pack is counted in it. Steel will be &b15&r iron and &b1&r carbon, bronze &b14&r copper and &b2&r tin: the sum is always sixteen, split according to the alloy's real composition.

And a Furnator, the furnace generator. Both machines from the starter chest run on FE and just sit there without power. Put it right next to the Dissolver and toss in coal: no cables needed, it feeds the neighboring block on its own. There's a second Furnator in the chest: put that one next to the Combiner, which eats three times as much.

Calcium will go into lime and redstone, aluminum into clay and obsidian, sulfur into acid, nitrogen into fertilizer. Sodium goes into salt: a compound of a metal that explodes in water and a gas that was used to poison soldiers in the trenches. Separately they're poisons; together they're something no living organism can do without.

Twelve elements carry the whole early game:
See the sights

A piston sits inside all five &6Alchemistry&r machines: the &eDissolver&r, the &eCombiner&r, the &eCompactor&r, the &eAtomizer&r and the Liquifier. Two of yours came from the chest, the third came as a reward, and everything else you'll have to build by hand, and every build starts with red dust.

And here a bed isn't about rest. First, it's your respawn point: the world is infinite and looks the same in every direction, and dying two thousand blocks from base means you no longer have a base. Second, three nights without sleep bring insomnia, and I wouldn't recommend meeting a phantom on an open plain to anyone, especially since nobody but the phantom makes membrane here.
So everything you build has to extract:
Until you have two sources, don't pour water anywhere you can't get it back from.
The sucrose recipe is written out here in full because it's not in JEI: it was removed from there so it wouldn't crash the client. The item itself works perfectly well.

There's a direct glass recipe in the Combiner, but it costs twice as much. This way is cheaper: the Combiner builds silicon dioxide from silicon and two oxygen, the Compactor presses four dioxide into sand, and a furnace turns sand into glass.

There's a chemical road to light too: &b4&r phosphorus and &b2&r oxygen give glowstone dust. Phosphorus comes in traces, a little over a percent, so one pinch is about three hundred and fifty dissolved blocks. Here are four atoms: see for yourself what a light source without wood costs.
The &eCombiner&r, from oxides. Check the exact composition in JEI: the recipe has been rewritten here, and the &6Alchemistry&r wiki gets it wrong.

The cheapest shelter in the game is the one you don't have to build. Two blocks down, step into the hole, plug the gap above your head with the same block you just dug out. Zero material spent, and all the rock goes back into your inventory in the morning.
Understand what you're actually doing here

You took &eantimatter&r apart into atoms and put it back together in exactly the same proportions, and got the same inert rock. Nothing lit up. So the problem isn't the composition: something is missing from it, and that something isn't in any of the elements you dug up today. It isn't in the periodic table at all. Not yet.

That's a dead end, and not your fault. The &eDissolver&r is made from iron. Iron comes from dissolving. Without the first machine nothing breaks the circle: not hard work, not time, not luck.

Then the obvious part: three paper and a leather make a book, books make bookshelves, bookshelves make enchanting. The &6Alchemistry&r book you're holding is restored the same way: a vanilla book and a stone pressure plate.
This branch is optional. But without it there will be no wood and no food in the world.

Sand, quartz and glass are the same substance, and the only difference is how it's packed. In quartz the atoms stand in a lattice; in glass the lattice didn't have time to form, because the melt cooled faster than the atoms could find their places. That's why in this pack one dioxide gives you sand, stone and glass.

Turn the percentages into blocks and you get an honest price list for this chapter. Iron: six blocks per atom. Carbon seven, silicon eight, oxygen ten, hydrogen twelve, calcium fourteen, aluminum seventeen, sulfur thirty-three, potassium sixty, phosphorus eighty, gold a hundred, platinum a thousand. From here on you can work out any price in the book yourself.
But wood brings everything you were missing: chests, sticks, torches, crafting tables, hoppers. This branch is optional only on paper.
Three wool and three planks. Wool is four string, the planks come from a grown tree, so a bed costs twelve spider strings and one log.

On the other hand, hiding is easier here than anywhere else. You can dig four blocks down, and any one of them is already under a roof. The first night is something you sit out, not something you win: you have no sword and won't have one by morning, because a stick needs wood and there's no wood in the world.

This is why you were saving calcium. The &eCombiner&r: iron oxide and calcium carbonate. Iron oxide is &b2&r iron and &b3&r oxygen, calcium carbonate is calcium plus carbonate, which is carbon with three oxygen. Ten atoms per pinch, six of them oxygen.
It can be claimed again and again, once every half hour. Use it as intended: the point is that one failure doesn't throw you out of the game, not that you never have to build machines.

The &eCompactor&r presses a handful of identical atoms into an item: &b16&r iron into dust, &b4&r silicon dioxide into sand, &b2&r graphite into coal. It doesn't transform anything, it only packs things tighter, but without it atoms stay atoms.

Not one of them is there for decoration. Magnesium, potassium and chlorine hold up obsidian, phosphorus holds up dirt and glowstone dust, strontium was the original base of redstone, nickel and zinc will go into alloys, and osmium is in the casing of every &6Mekanism&r machine: without it, chapter two doesn't even start. Platinum is a tenth of a percent, and you'll need around a thousand atoms of it for a single reactor casing.

One bucket can't make an infinite source: for new water to appear in an empty cell, it needs two sources next to it. With one bucket you're only moving water from place to place and losing it with every mistake.

You don't have to build it with chemistry, but it's worth knowing the price: the Combiner makes wool from a triglyceride and two keratin, which is about three and a half thousand blocks per white cube. Twelve strings from spiders versus forty thousand dissolved blocks of rock: that's the whole argument for why this world has mobs.

You can see the difference with sand. The &eCompactor&r takes four silicon dioxide and gives you sand. The &eCombiner&r asks eight for the very same sand. And it's like that for all the loose stuff: in the Combiner it costs exactly twice as much, because the Compactor's job isn't to discover anything new but to make the old things half as expensive.
Next comes energy. A coal furnace is a campfire, and the next chapter starts precisely with no longer burning something that cost sixty blocks a lump.

It's here for the feeling. In the Core chapter you'll learn to fuse nuclei, and copper, number &b29&r, plus tin, number &b50&r, will give you element number &b79&r. The transmutation people hunted for six hundred years will turn out cheaper than sifting through fifteen hundred blocks.

String is pressed from one keratin. Keratin is &b2&r protein, &b2&r starch and &b5&r sulfur dioxide. Protein is ethylene, ammonia, sulfur and carbon dioxide. Starch is &b12&r carbon, &b20&r hydrogen, &b10&r oxygen. Convert all of it into blocks using the Dissolver's percentages, and a single string comes out at about fifteen hundred dissolved blocks of rock. A gold ingot costs the same.
Everything that walks is raw material

Each row rolls on its own, so one block can drop iron and carbon at the same time, or nothing at all, and that happens with roughly every third block. On average a block gives about one atom. An iron ingot is &b16&r atoms, so around a hundred dissolved blocks. Remember that order of magnitude, it will keep coming up the whole game.

That's the whole joke of the pack: &6you're standing on the goal from minute one and you can't take it&r. All you can do is break it down into atoms and build it up again, more and more elaborately, until you understand what it's missing.
You're not the one who mines iron. You're the one who &lTAKES IT APART&r.
&8You're goddamn right.

Make 2 pistons

Dead rock

The &eDissolver&r works in probabilities: each row of its table rolls separately, and whatever drops, drops. The &eCombiner&r works by formula: the composition has to match down to the atom, or it simply won't start. The &eCompactor&r doesn't count anything: one substance in, one item out, no reaction.

One bone on a crafting table gives three bone meal, and you don't need any chemistry for it. There's a chemical route too, two hydroxylapatite in the Compactor give the same three, but there's no reason to pay eight hundred blocks for something a skeleton carries around with it.
&aThis quest unlocks the “Energy” chapter.&r
Don't build storerooms or walls out of rock. Every block in a wall is atoms you'll be short of later for water.
Botany without botany

You've had the first one from the very start; what you need is a second. An empty bucket is three iron ingots, and one already came as a reward; the Combiner builds a water bucket from an empty bucket and &b16&r units of water.
&6Thermal&r: a Servo on the output side of the duct.

On the left of the interface there's a button with a list of recipes. Click the one you want and it locks in: the &eCombiner&r will wait for exactly its ingredients, whatever else is sitting in the input. Without the lock the machine picks a recipe from the slot contents on its own; you can go back to that by removing the lock with the button at the top.
R and U

Hydrogen drops eight times out of a hundred, and it's the scarcest element in the rock. Don't waste it on experiments: there's no water in the world at all (no lakes, no rain, no ice), and everything that will ever need it, from farms to reactor cooling, comes down to this recipe.

Humanity found copper before it invented writing, because copper occurs in native form and doesn't need to be smelted from ore. An entire age is named after what you get when you add a little tin to it. Here, neither one is just lying under your feet.

You've already met the twelve common elements. Below them in the Dissolver's table there are thirteen more rows, and all together they make up less than one chance in ten: magnesium, potassium, phosphorus, titanium, chlorine, manganese, strontium, zinc, tin, nickel, osmium, silver, platinum.
One more thing: the task will take the sixteen blocks for good. Build them from atoms instead of handing over ones you dug up: the point is to go all the way around the circle once.
The machine that doesn't do chemistry
Fix: no machines left
A branch for patience, and the most expensive thing in the chapter. The &eCompactor&r, a furnace, no secret, just time.
The &eCompactor&r turns &b16&r atoms into iron dust, a furnace turns that into a regular ingot. Fuel comes from the chest for now.

And one thing worth getting used to right away: purity here isn't a figure of speech. An atom is either the right one or a different one, there's no third option. Iron with a gold impurity isn't ninety-nine percent iron, it's two different items in two different slots.
A bone dissolves into hydroxylapatite, the mineral part of real bone, Ca₅(PO₄)₃OH. It drops in half the attempts, but three at a time.

Mobs spawn where the block light level is zero: not “dark to the eye”, but exactly zero. A torch gives light level fourteen and clears a circle about seven blocks in radius. Marking out your area in a grid is cheaper than finding out later what has moved in behind your back.
With bone meal a sapling shoots up in a few clicks instead of a few minutes. And since a tree means planks, sticks, torches, paper and a bed, this is exactly where all the night work pays off.

A side branch whose whole point is not throwing away the rare stuff while you dig for the common stuff. By the time you need calcium, sodium, aluminum, sulfur and nitrogen, it will be too late to start stockpiling them.
The most expensive fuel in the world
So here's a spare kit: a Dissolver and a &eCombiner&r, exactly what was in the chest at spawn. With that pair, you can build the &eCompactor&r yourself.
Notice what's not in the recipe. Lava. Not a single drop of lava exists in this world, and obsidian is by definition solidified lava. You're making cold what nature only ever makes hot.
A tree out of nothing
Make 4 Nether Quartz

Take the generator and the Dissolver underground with you. An explosion in a world four blocks thick doesn't bury anyone, but it's perfectly good at carrying off a machine along with everything inside it, and a second Dissolver can only be made from steel.
Sideways the world is infinite; downward it's four blocks and then &ebedrock&r. There's nothing to dig down for, so you can only grow outward and upward.
Make 8 coal

Four string on a crafting table give wool, three wool make a bed, three string and three sticks make a bow. In this world a spider isn't a nuisance, it's a spinning mill, and it works the night shift.
There's a direct log recipe too, and it costs exactly as much as a sapling. It's not an alternative, it's an emergency exit: a sapling grows into a whole tree, while a log stays a log.

Quartz is the same SiO₂, its third form after sand and glass: the same lattice, but regular and intact, which is why quartz has facets and glass doesn't. Technology needs it not for its looks but for the piezoelectric effect: squeeze the crystal and a voltage appears on its faces; apply a voltage and it squeezes itself. Every quartz watch and every clock generator in a processor runs on this.
Here's the &6Alchemistry&r book: it has the mod's machines and multiblock diagrams. If you lose it, craft a new one from a vanilla book and a stone pressure plate.
Kaolinite: &b2&r silicon dioxide, aluminum oxide, &b2&r water.
By hand or with the starter pickaxe: the rock is soft and doesn't need a proper tool. It's only four blocks deep here, so there's exactly one direction, and infinity lies that way.

Today you won't place anything with these pistons: the second line of machines is locked behind steel ingots, and steel is chapter three. Start stockpiling anyway. Redstone comes from calcium and oxygen, and oxygen, after hydrogen, is the tightest bottleneck of the early game, so a reserve of it builds up slowly.
&6Alchemistry&r machines don't push anything out anywhere. There's a toggle in the interface, but the output has to be pulled from outside: the machine will never put anything into a pipe by itself.
Red dust without strontium
Open JEI and get used to living in it
Dig sideways

The rule of this pack: everything is built from atoms. Mobs are the only exception, and it works in your favor. They bring things the rock doesn't give at all, and they bring them themselves, for free.
Have 32 torches on hand

This one is given to you, not crafted, and generosity has nothing to do with it. The pack has to hand out the first machines: the &eDissolver&r is made of iron, iron comes from dissolving, and that circle doesn't break on its own. A second &eCompactor&r you'll have to build yourself, and that takes steel, which is chapter three.

Chemistry is the study of change. Not of substances as such, but of transitions: growth, decay, then growth again. That's how it's defined in the first lecture of any course, and that's how the two boxes from your starter chest work.
A utility quest. It's for exactly one situation: you've been left without your starter machines.

Seventeen atoms per ball, about a hundred and ninety blocks: twice the price of an iron ingot. Nine of the seventeen atoms are oxygen, and that eats up half the price; the four hydrogen from the two waters add another quarter. Clay in a world without water is expensive by construction.

The &eDissolver&r is decay. The &eCombiner&r is growth. Everything else in this pack, including twelve chapters and the last item in the game, is those same two operations, chained together enough times.

That's how the whole pack works, and, frankly, all of physics: taking things apart is always cheaper than putting them together. Order is lost on its own and comes back only through work done from outside.
Put a Furnator next to it, it runs on FE too.

The second bucket changes the status of water forever. Place two sources with one cell between them, and you never count liters again. A bucket is &b48&r atoms, &b32&r of them hydrogen, so around four hundred dissolved blocks. The only thing pricier in this chapter is gold.
Here's a sword. You've already done this barehanded; no need to keep it up.
Have two water buckets at the same time
Quartz. But not today

Obsidian is solidified volcanic glass, a mixture rather than a compound: mostly silica, followed by oxides of aluminum, sodium and iron. The last one is what makes it black; the glass from the neighboring quest is the same silica, just without it.
Pull, don't wait
From there it's just like a normal game: dirt on the floor, sapling on the dirt, light from above.
Make your first obsidian
The bottom of the list
The bread from the chest won't last long, and there's no other food in the world.
H₂O. Literally
A hole in the world

Two small things for later. Witches are rare, but they drink potions faster than you can land hits. And better not stare at an enderman: it never rains in this biome, there's no water in the world, and the one weakness everybody is used to counting on doesn't work here.
One oxygen and two hydrogen. That's not two ingredients because some designer decided so; it's the formula, and in this pack the proportions in recipes mean exactly what they mean in chemistry.
Make 4 iron ingots
Make 8 redstone

A pipe that waits for the machine to put things into it won't work. I'm telling you up front, because otherwise you'll find out about two hours in, staring at a clogged output slot and an empty chest.
SiO₂
The &eCompactor&r: &b16&r atoms into copper dust, the dust into a furnace. Copper is &b4&r percent of the rock, so an ingot comes to about four hundred blocks.

The &eCombiner&r: &b6&r carbon, &b10&r hydrogen, &b5&r oxygen. C₆H₁₀O₅ is the building block of the most common organic polymer on the planet; chains of it make up plant cell walls, which means all wood, all grass and all paper at once.
Count by oxygen, not silicon: you use twice as much oxygen, and it drops less often. Silicon will pile up in surplus; get used to it, that won't change later on.
And it's just as dead.

Along the way you'll discover that the &eCombiner&r can build more than water out of hydrogen and oxygen. Hydroxide, OH, is the same two elements, just with one hydrogen instead of two. The machine sees both in its slots and takes whichever recipe it finds first, and the one it finds first isn't always the one you need.

A rule for the whole game: recipes in JEI outrank any text, both this book and the &6Alchemistry&r wiki. Half of the mod's recipes have been rewritten here for a world without ores, and JEI shows the rewritten ones.
Later on, phosphorus will go into dirt, glowstone dust and bone meal. Until the Periodic Table chapter it exists in this world in exactly one form: on two legs, carrying a bow.

Rotten flesh is protein. Bone is calcium phosphate. String is keratin. Gunpowder is sulfur, saltpeter and graphite. An ender pearl is silicon, mercury and neodymium, and there isn't a single atom of mercury or neodymium in the rock.

Now the price. Building one hydroxylapatite from elements takes &b5&r calcium, &b2&r hydroxide and &b6&r phosphate, and each phosphate is one phosphorus and four oxygen. Phosphorus is a little over a percent of the rock, and that's where it all falls apart: about eight hundred and fifty blocks apiece. A skeleton gives three and walks them over to you itself.
Walls on the surface are both pricier and worse. A spider climbs over, a creeper takes them apart, and every block in a wall is atoms you'll be short of later for water.
Craft a bed
Get 4 ender pearls

Further along the branch there's a quest for each drop, and each one works out how many blocks the same thing would cost if you made it honestly. The numbers are indecent. Treat the night not as a nuisance but as a shift at the factory.
The sun is going down
Make 16 sand and compare both recipes in JEI

Hence a rule for the whole game. If there's a Compactor recipe, use the Compactor. Leave the &eCombiner&r for what the Compactor can't do: it's the only one that builds an item from different substances rather than from one.
Phosphorus walks on two legs

There's no sugar cane in the world, but there is the Dissolver, and it breaks any log into exactly one cellulose. With a grown tree, paper comes at one sheet per log. Without a tree it's two hundred-plus dissolved blocks per sheet, because cellulose has ten hydrogen, and hydrogen is the scarcest element in the rock.
The &eCompactor&r: one cellulose, one sheet. The &eCombiner&r asks two for the same thing, so after chapter three paper gets half as expensive all by itself.
There's nothing to speed it up with. Bone meal comes down to phosphorus, and phosphorus shows up in the rock only in traces, so it's cheaper to just wait, like on day one of a vanilla game.
Dissolve your way to 512 iron
Sapling: &b2&r cellulose and oxygen.
Make 16 water in the Combiner
Obsidian without lava
Count what you got. Thirty-two atoms for four blocks, and to dig up that many you'll have to dissolve about a hundred. Twenty-odd blocks of the world for every one you put back.

And one habit worth dropping right away: don't shift-click the ingredient transfer button in the Combiner and the Compactor, because afterwards your inventory falls out of sync with the server. A normal click is fine, as often as you like.
No water, no lava, no wood, no stone, no sand, no grass, no ores, no villages, no caves. There is a sky, and nothing grows under it. That's it, the tour is over.

There are twenty-four in the chest, and no more will turn up. A torch is coal and a stick, a stick is a plank, a plank is a log, and a log grows from a sapling that the Combiner builds from cellulose. So light in this world comes down to botany, and that's not a joke, it's the order of operations.
Make one gold ingot

The mod originally had this recipe on strontium carbonate, and strontium is six tenths of a percent of the rock: you'd never stock up enough for redstone. Here strontium has been replaced with calcium. The iron oxide stayed, though: it's hematite, the classic red ochre, and it's what gives the color. The swap isn't free (it's strontium that burns with a red flame, while calcium gives orange), but otherwise chapter one would have hit a wall.
The Copper Age

A threat too, mind you. There are no thunderstorms in this biome, so you won't see charged ones, but the regular kind is plenty: it doesn't blow a hole through the world, it just carries off the Furnator, the Dissolver and everything inside them. Fight at range, or don't fight at all.
Make 4 apples

Kaolinite is two silicon dioxide, aluminum oxide and two water. That's literally the formula of clay, Al₂Si₂O₅(OH)₄, and the water in it isn't a solvent but part of the crystal: you can only drive it out by destroying the mineral. The &eCompactor&r presses kaolinite into a ball, and the ball is fired into a brick.
The only mercury in the world
What the world is made of
Now look at the block you made. The composition checks out. The arithmetic checks out. It's indistinguishable from what lies under your feet for a thousand kilometers in every direction.
Hover over an item and press R to see how to get it, U to see what it's used in. &6ChemLib&r elements and compounds have their own tab: it shows the formula and what the substance is built from.
1 · Dust
Collect 16 bones
Dissolve rock: 8 iron and 8 carbon
You are standing on the answer

By day the plain looks harmless. At night it turns out there's nowhere on it to hide: no hill, no tree, no wall, and the number of dark blocks around you is exactly infinity. Zombies, skeletons, spiders and creepers spawn right in the middle of the field, and there's nowhere to run from them, because the field looks the same everywhere.
Collect 24 string

And remember the word “porcelain.” Kaolin is its raw material, and porcelain has a reputation for being chemically resistant. For anyone who someday has to store hydrofluoric acid, that reputation will come back to bite them, but that belongs to the acids chapter, not this one.

One “no” is missing from that list, and it's not forgetfulness: &cthere are mobs here&r. The rock doesn't glow, there's nowhere to hide on the plain, and darkness brings zombies, skeletons, spiders and creepers. The branch above the starting quest covers the first night.
Twenty-four torches, and that's it

There's twice as much hydrogen here as everything else combined, and hydrogen is nearly the rarest thing in the rock. Four cellulose is forty hydrogen atoms, five hundred blocks. Organic matter is expensive in a dead world, as it should be.
Make 4 cellulose

An apple made of sugar and fiber is a simplification, but not a fabrication: by dry mass, that's roughly what the fruit consists of. The other eighty-five percent of an apple is water, and the mod graciously doesn't count it.
Collect 8 gunpowder
Sulfur will later go into acids, saltpeter into fertilizer, and both are almost out of reach in chapter one. So the green guy is less a threat than a walking warehouse of scarce goods.

Further down the list there are thirteen more, from magnesium to platinum, at tenths of a percent. They do drop, but you can't live on them: they're not a steady flow, they're a reason to build a bigger Dissolver.
In this world &cthere is no ore&r. There's only a man who learned to get matter without leaving his basement.
Three planks, four cobblestone, an iron ingot and a pinch of redstone. The recipe is vanilla; the only unusual thing is where it ends up.

“A tree out of nothing” says there's nothing to speed up growth with: bone meal comes down to phosphorus, and phosphorus only shows up in traces. That was the plain truth, right up until the first night.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.02_energy.0: Get 2 Osmium Ingots
Now about the price. Our coal is four graphite, that is sixteen carbon atoms pulled out of the rock and never returned. Charcoal is a log from a tree you grew, and it costs one smelting.
&b1&r carbon + &b3&r oxygen → carbonate;
Sixteen silver atoms are, on average, more than ten thousand dissolved blocks. Don't sit over the Dissolver, build an Enricher: its concentrate has twenty times more silver than the same rock.
Grow 16 brown mushrooms
A sapling needs a light level of at least &b9&r. The rock glows on its own, but faintly: stick a torch next to it.

Count how much you've already burned. Every element dust into an ingot, every brick, every pane of glass, every piece of charcoal: all of it paid for with carbon from the rock. The Energized Smelter shifts the cost from matter to power, and your power is now exactly as renewable as wood is.
A Basic cube surrounded by four Infused Alloy, two tablets and two osmium ingots. And so on for every next tier: the previous cube in the middle, the new tier's alloy in the corners.
Six planks instead of four
Stage fix: energy
Power here isn't “the next tech tier”. Without it, nothing that takes the world apart into atoms will turn, and taking the world apart is the only way to get anything in it at all.

So why have it? Because heat can be carried through a conductor to where there's nothing to burn. The Fuelwood Heater makes sense for the same reason: it burns coal in one place and heats a generator in another, and the workshop stops being tied to the stove.

Factories come in eight kinds, one for every machine that works item by item: enriching, smelting, crushing, sawing, compressing, infusing, injecting, purifying. In this world the first four make sense.
Second on the same casing is the Energized Smelter: the same set, just glass instead of iron. It smelts on power instead of coal and takes the carbon cost off every dust.

&b24&r silicon dioxide, &b8&r aluminum oxide, &b8&r magnesium oxide, &b8&r potassium chloride and &b16&r graphite. Magnesium, potassium and chlorine: all three from the tail of the table, all three in one recipe. The first line in the chapter that runs into not one rare element but three at once.
Three steps, and this is the real contact process, the way sulfuric acid has been made since the late nineteenth century:
A multiblock four to eighteen blocks tall: the taller the tower, the faster the evaporation. A controller, valves for input and output, and everything else is plain Thermal Evaporation Blocks.
Stage energy (again)

In &6Mekanism&r a furnace isn't furniture, it's an ingredient: you craft it and feed it to the crafting table. Until you have an Energized Smelter, it's also the only way to turn element dust into an ingot.

There's one trap and it's a classic: a network is rated by its worst section. One basic segment accidentally left in an ultimate line throttles the whole line down to &b3&r,&b200&r. If power isn't reaching somewhere, don't look for a breakdown, look for that one piece you couldn't be bothered to replace.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.02_energy.1: Make 8 each of Advanced and Elite cables

A shovel goes the other way and turns the dirt into a dirt path. A path grows things half as fast, a multiplier of &b0.5&r. The only way in this pack to make things worse for yourself with a single click.

First the Electrolytic Core: &b5&r Infused Alloy, &b2&r osmium dust, an iron dust, a gold dust. Then the separator itself: &b4&r iron, &b2&r redstone, &b2&r alloy and the core. Pour the water in with a bucket, that one and only bucket.
&aYou don't have to pick osmium out of the rock grain by grain:&r concentrate from the Enricher gives it twenty times faster, with three hundred times less work for the Dissolver.

Fe₆₄Ni₃₆. The name comes from “invariant”: the alloy has almost zero thermal expansion and doesn't change size when heated. Charles Guillaume got the &b1920&r Nobel Prize in Physics for it, not for an elegant theory but because clock pendulums stopped lying every time the weather changed.
Craft a Heat Generator and run it on coal
&b100&r SO₃ and &b100&r water vapor: &b100&r mB of acid.
One tank for hydrogen, one for oxygen, and the separator will finally stop halting every thirty seconds.
“Enrichment” here is an honest word, not a reaction: the same substance, packed denser. That's exactly how ore and uranium are enriched.

In the Combiner, straight from elements: iron and carbon for the steel, osmium for the frame, silicon and oxygen for the glass. The mod's normal recipe (&b4&r steel ingots, &b4&r glass and an osmium ingot) works too, but the steel ingot as a separate item only shows up in chapter three, and you need the casing now.

Now hover over the &eCombiner&r: &b200&r FE/t. One Heat Generator can't cover even half of that, and that's not a balance mistake, it's a difference of schools: one mod counts energy generously, the other stingily. The Dissolver is more modest, &b60&r FE/t: one generator feeds it with room to spare.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.02_energy.2: Craft a Chemical Oxidizer
Wood, in parts
One obsidian through four machines
If the stage didn't arrive
Solar and Advanced Solar: they need open sky and daytime. There's no sun over the ash, and by design there won't be: free energy would zero out the whole chapter. Removed.
You can also make a mushroom in the Combiner: phosphoric acid plus chitin. The difference is that the recipe takes phosphorus every time, and the pot takes it once.

That's why ore isn't dissolved whole, it's &lenriched&r. Ground up, mixed with water, and the heavy part separates from the waste. The &eEnricher&r does exactly that: &b16&r blocks of &eWhite Antimatter&r and &b250&r mB of water give one &eTrace Concentrate&r.
Check what the rock is made of

If something else is dropping out, you need the fix from another chapter. Chapter &b2&r: the &eAtomizer&r, the &eLiquifier&r and the Industrial tiers of &6Alchemistry&r machines. Chapter &b3&r: the ME Controller, the Molecular Assembler and the Pattern Provider. Chapter &b4&r: the Cascade tiers of &6Alchemistry&r machines and everything for the fission reactor. Chapter &b5&r: the Fusion Chamber Controller and the Fusion Core, the &eQuantum Compressor&r. Chapter &b6&r: the Ultimate tables from &6Extended Crafting&r. Chapter &b7&r: the Antimatter Shard and &eAntimatter&r itself.
Not in a pot. A tuber gives back one to two, plus a fifteen percent chance of a second roll. A planted potato pays for itself in the first cycle and feeds you for free after that.
No. &b76&r, &b22&r.&b59&r g/cm³: the densest naturally occurring substance, twice as dense as lead.
Make 24 Deepslate blocks
There are no skeletons in this world and there won't be, so phosphorus from the tail of the table is the only source of bones, period. Spend it on speeding up things that grow slowly, not wheat.
&b8&r gold + &b8&r silver. The rock gives gold &b1&r%% of the time, the rarest element on the list, and eight atoms per ingot is something you feel physically.

Of the whole &6Thermal&r series, the pack has only Foundation: materials without machines. It provides eight metals: tin, lead, nickel, silver, bronze, constantan, electrum, invar. Plus ruby and sapphire.

The only alloy of these three that occurs in nature ready-made: native gold almost always comes with silver. The first coins in history, the Lydian ones, were struck from electrum, not out of any noble intent but because nobody could separate gold from silver back then.
Three slots instead of one
Grant the stage again
The sawmill draws &b20&r FE/t, the same as the electric furnace. Only the pots themselves are cheaper in this chapter.
The installer is a tier upgrade applied to a factory that's already placed. Right-click the block, and Basic becomes Advanced without being taken apart or losing its contents.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.02_energy.3: A mushroom in the Metallurgic Infuser's infusion tank gives ten units of fungi infusion. A dirt block plus ten units makes mycelium.

The mod has its own way: Obsidian Dust plus osmium gas in the Osmium Compressor. It's cheaper in elements and more expensive in machines: the compressor still has to be built, and it's further down the map.
A Nobel for standing still
The tier changes in place
A furnace that doesn't eat
Mushrooms grow on stone
Craft a Resistive Heater

The second recipe works and doesn't ask for a charge. A copper dust and a nickel dust give two constantan dust, three copper and a tin give four bronze, two iron and a nickel give three invar. Dust into the furnace, ingot out.
a sulfur dust in the Oxidizer: &b100&r mB of SO₂;
Make 4 hay bales
The way into Mekanism

A next-tier circuit is the previous circuit between two alloys of the previous tier. Basic plus two Infused makes Advanced. Advanced plus two Reinforced makes Elite. Elite plus two Atomic makes Ultimate. One pattern for the whole ladder, only the filling changes.
The Enrichment Chamber needs two, the Energized Smelter two, and further up the tiers it only gets more.
Craft a Botany Pot

The Enrichment Chamber does more than redstone. It makes Enriched Carbon from coal, Enriched Gold and Enriched Tin from dust, Enriched Diamond from diamond, and Enriched Obsidian from Refined Obsidian Dust.
The takeaway for the whole chapter: you need not one generator but a whole row. One for the Dissolver, three for the Combiner, and that's before any margin for scaling up.

It's also the answer to the question you've surely asked by now: you can assemble a finished casing from atoms, but you can't cast a steel ingot yet. Taking apart and putting together is easier than forging.
A diamond in this pack is five hundred and twelve carbon atoms through a press. Four alloys per stone isn't generosity, it's the only price at which this tier is passable at all.

Sixteen atoms per ingot, like everything else in the pack. None of the three is much use on its own: tin goes into bronze and the Filter Upgrade, nickel into invar and constantan, silver into electrum and, well, more electrum.

Thirteen lines, and the whole chapter rests on them. Redstone stands on strontium, obsidian on magnesium, potassium and chlorine, bone meal on phosphorus, every &6Mekanism&r machine on osmium, every alloy on tin, nickel and silver.
The mod's only interpreter between liquid and gas. Liquid tank on the left, gas tank on the right, direction switch on top.
Waste rock to the dump

Capacity in FE: &b1&r,&b600&r,&b000&r, then &b6&r,&b400&r,&b000&r, then &b25&r,&b600&r,&b000&r, then &b102&r,&b400&r,&b000&r. Output: &b1&r,&b600&r FE/t, &b6&r,&b400&r, &b25&r,&b600&r, &b102&r,&b400&r. Exactly fourfold at every step, and capacity and output grow together.
A plant instead of a torch
&b8&r cobbled deepslate per furnace. You start with one, and you'll need at least three: one goes into the Heat Generator, two into the Metallurgic Infuser.
A potato is four potassium and a starch. A carrot is beta-carotene and cellulose. In the Combiner each one is a one-off purchase: the next one costs exactly as much as the first.

Five terracotta and a flower pot. Terracotta is a fired clay block, a clay block is four kaolinite clay balls, and a flower pot is three bricks made from the same balls. Twenty-three balls per pot, and in the end all of them are silicon, aluminum and water.
Make 16 bone meal
The machine's name is more honest than it looks. S + O₂ → SO₂ is literally sulfur burning, and in industry the first step of making sulfuric acid looks exactly the same.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.02_energy.4: Eight cables of one tier around a single alloy make eight cables of the next tier. Infused Alloy gives Advanced, Reinforced gives Elite, Atomic gives Ultimate.

Gold in electronics is the real thing: contacts are gold-plated not for conductivity (copper and silver conduct better) but because gold doesn't oxidize at all. Twenty years later a gold-plated contact is still a contact; any other one gets overgrown with an oxide film.
There's no other fuel here. Firewood in commercial quantities is a long way off, there's no lava at all, and gas only arrives near the end of the chapter.

The pot looks not at the item but at the soil category. Dirt counts as dirt, sand as sand, deepslate as stone, a hay bale as mulch. What fits what is shown in the Crops tab in JEI, and that's where to start with any new pot, so you don't burn elements on guesswork.
Gears and plates need the press from &6Thermal&r Expansion, and Expansion isn't in the pack. The rule is simple: if a JEI recipe goes through a machine you've never seen, that machine isn't coming.

Two strips of steel with redstone between them make eight cables. In &6Mekanism&r steel is the foundation of everything that transfers: cables, pipes, tubes and transporters are all crafted on the same pattern, and only what goes in the middle changes.

Throughput in FE per tick: Basic &b3&r,&b200&r, Advanced &b51&r,&b200&r, Elite &b409&r,&b600&r, Ultimate &b3&r,&b276&r,&b800&r. The step from the first to the second is sixteenfold, after that eightfold.

Unpack it and count what it cost: one basic circuit, six Infused Alloy, four Reinforced, two Atomic. In atoms that's osmium, gold, strontium, carbon for two diamonds, magnesium, potassium and chlorine. One circuit board has gathered almost the entire tail of the table.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.02_energy.5: A dirt block, a sapling on top, a torch beside it. Then you wait: there's no bone meal, bones would first have to be taken from someone, and at night that's a fair fight.

And this is where the real price kicks in. Lithium only comes from the evaporation plant: ten buckets of water give one bucket of brine, ten buckets of brine give one of lithium. A hundred millibuckets of lithium is enough for one dust. Do the math: about ten buckets of water per dust, four dusts per cell.
From this point on, organics stop costing atoms. Everything you used to make one at a time in the Combiner now grows on its own: you pay once, for the first seed.

Remember this spot. You're standing on the answer, you took it apart down to the atoms and found out there aren't enough atoms. Chapter six will be about exactly that, and the first crack showed up in the most harmless chapter of all, the one about electricity.
Make 8 Invar Ingots
Click the checkmark and claim the reward, and the stage will be granted again. If you already have it, nothing changes: granting it twice is harmless.
Each has its own capacity. A basic-tier pipe holds &b2&r,&b000&r mB, a gas tube &b4&r,&b000&r, and a transporter moves one item at a time. The same four tiers, upgraded with the same alloys.

The rule is the same for all of them: the enriched version carries &b80&r units of infusion instead of &b10&r. Exactly eight times, no exceptions. This is the main multiplier of the whole mod, the only place where one item gives more than was put into it.
And the other way around too. For water to become water vapor for the acid, it needs exactly this block.

Until now food was an expense on par with iron: no farms, no livestock, apples made from sucrose and cellulose. The pot solves hunger for good, and hunger is the first problem it takes off your plate.
Practical payoff right away: Refined Obsidian and Refined Glowstone come out noticeably cheaper through the compressor than through the Combiner.

The Heat Generator puts out &b200&r J/t, that is &b80&r FE/t. The Enrichment Chamber, the Infuser and the Energized Smelter each want &b50&r J/t, that is &b20&r FE/t. One generator feeds four &6Mekanism&r machines without breaking a sweat.
Redstone ×8
The generator pushes energy straight into the adjacent block, so you don't need cables at first: just place the machine right next to it.

Gas isn't an item. It won't go through an item pipe and won't fit in a chest: you need a Pressurized Tube and a Chemical Tank. For the first time in the whole pack, a hopper under the generator is useless.
Nice and dense

Nine wheat make a hay bale. In a pot a hay bale counts as mulch, a multiplier of &b1&r.&b05&r, the same as tilled farmland. The difference is that farmland has to be tilled, while the bale you simply grew.
Eighty for two alloys. So one block of obsidian, run through four machines, covers the top of the ladder.
A casing, &b2&r tablets, &b2&r iron, &b4&r Infused Alloy.
No bones, but bone meal
And every &6Draconic Evolution&r Wyvern Core has two Elite Control Circuits in it, and the endgame needs thousands of Wyvern Cores. You'll have to put this circuit on a production line.
Got it
The tower that drinks

What it does: turns an osmium ingot into two hundred millibuckets of osmium gas and then blows that gas into dust. For the first time in the pack, a metal stops being an item and becomes a gas, and that's exactly the mechanic the whole nuclear line will ride on later.
&6Mekanism&r has a shortcut too: toss a sulfur dust straight into the acid tank and you get &b2&r mB. The long way gives a hundred from the same dust. Fifty times more, for two extra machines.
Make 2 saplings
Grow a tree and get 16 planks
This isn't a convenience. It's the only way to grow anything in this world more than once.

A full cycle is &b1,200&r ticks, exactly one minute. The dirt block is never used up, and the seeds come back with the harvest five percent of the time, which is enough: wheat drops one or two at a time anyway.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.02_energy.6: Get a Steel Casing
An Elite Control Circuit between two Atomic Alloy. The top of the ladder; the mod has nothing beyond it.
&b4&r iron, &b2&r furnaces, &b2&r redstone, &b1&r osmium ingot. The machine needs power, so place it right against the generator.
C₆H₁₀O₅. Half of any wood is made of this, which is why all the organics in this chapter rest on cellulose: the sapling, the dirt, the planks. Count with a margin.
Craft 3 furnaces
The index of industry
Check in JEI what drops from White Antimatter

Mushrooms are the only thing that grows on bare stone, and in a world without dirt that matters more than it sounds. Stew, furnace fuel and, most importantly, fungi infusion for the Metallurgic Infuser, which we'll come back to below.

A tube is a buffer in itself, and that's handier than it sounds: a long run holds a reserve of gas as well as a small tank does. The Universal Cable works exactly the same way; people just usually don't notice the buffer there.
A log on a crafting table gives four planks. A log in the sawmill gives six, plus a 25%% chance of sawdust.

One Enriched Redstone gives the Infuser &b80&r units instead of &b10&r. The rock gives six tenths of a percent strontium, and &6Mekanism&r wants redstone by the stack, so build the chamber right away, not when you're already squeezed.
Make an Ultimate Control Circuit

Gas is neither an item nor a liquid, it has its own vessels. Tanks: Basic &b64&r,&b000&r mB, Advanced &b256&r,&b000&r, Elite &b1&r,&b024&r,&b000&r, Ultimate &b8&r,&b192&r,&b000&r. Pressurized Tubes: &b4&r,&b000&r, &b16&r,&b000&r, &b256&r,&b000&r, &b1&r,&b024&r,&b000&r.
The deepslate you've been stamping out by the block since the start of the chapter is soil of two categories at once, stone and mushroom. So a pot of it takes mushrooms, both colors.
The Muffling Upgrade is no joke: &6Mekanism&r is noisy, and a workshop of thirty machines is unbearably noisy.
Three steps in the Combiner:
Make 4 Basic Control Circuits
Like any &6ChemLib&r metal: &b16&r osmium atoms → &eCompactor&r → dust → furnace → ingot.
Make 2 each of Speed and Energy Upgrades
An interpreter between liquid and gas

So in this pack the renewable fuel isn't just cheaper than the non-renewable one, it's also twice as effective wherever infusion units are counted. The tree from the chapter's third quest pays off a second time.
The metal that became a gas
Take an Enrichment Chamber, surround it with alloys and circuits, and you get a factory. The same recipe, only three slots instead of one, with a shared energy buffer and control panel.
That adds up to &b90&r%%, so roughly one roll in ten comes up empty. That's intended.
The world heats itself
Coal gives the Infuser &b10&r units of carbon. Charcoal gives &b20&r. Twice as much for the same space in the tank.

The concentrate has no iron and no carbon, only the rare stuff: osmium, tin, nickel, silver, zinc. The Dissolver breaks it down as usual. An osmium ingot takes &b20&r concentrates, that is &b320&r blocks instead of &b6,400&r, and three hundred times less work for the Dissolver.
The soil goes in a slot
Well, stone
You can't get here too early: the fix only unlocks after the quest that grants the stage in the first place.
The fission and fusion reactors need water for cooling. Lots of water. You have one bucket.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.02_energy.7: &7You get fewer atoms out than the rock had in it: the waste rock goes to the dump. That's the fair price for the rare stuff.&r
Gas needs its own vessels
The casing is cheap: four steel and an Energy Tablet give four of them at once. The cell and the provider, though, want Lithium Dust.
Craft a Metallurgic Infuser
Forty buckets of water per cell
Make 8 Constantan Ingots
Infused Alloy, the Basic Control Circuit and Steel Dust all pass through the Infuser. Without it, the mod consists of one generator and nothing else.
You can, by the way. You have a Combiner.
Solid becomes gas
Mix 2 Constantan Dust on a crafting table
From here on, hands won't cut it. The &eDissolver&r and the Combiner are machines, and &6machines don't run on enthusiasm&r.
What it does: water to brine, brine to lithium, at a hundred to one at each step. As a by-product, brine gives salt, and salt is sodium and chlorine, your way into chlorine chemistry.
Three trace elements in one line
Read and move on
The only thing that grows here
The Heat Generator needs two planks, and there's nowhere else to get them. Along the way you'll get sticks, chests and crafting tables in commercial quantities.

Thirty-two is enough to get started and definitely not enough after that: &6Mekanism&r eats redstone by the bucket. The Enrichment Chamber at the end of the chapter raises the yield eightfold, and that's not an optimization, it's a necessity.
A day of work in one block
&b2&r iron + &b3&r oxygen → iron oxide;
First power: carbon you dug out from under your own feet
Collect 16 coal
It takes redstone not as a recipe ingredient but as infusion fuel, into a separate tank: one redstone is &b10&r units, an alloy costs &b10&r, a circuit &b20&r.
The first food that costs no atoms
&b4&r redstone, &b3&r gold, &b2&r Infused Alloy.
Twelve. The periodic table has a hundred and eighteen. This isn't “not enough ore”: the other hundred and six are physically not in the rock.
Osmium ingot into the Infuser, redstone into the tank. Twenty units per circuit, twice the cost of an alloy, and the osmium goes in as whole ingots.
There is no ore to multiply
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.02_energy.8: Make 32 redstone
The other half of every recipe
It isn't here. There isn't a single ore in this world: no veins, no blocks, no raw chunks. Nothing to multiply.
Craft a stone hoe and till the dirt right in the pot
Point at a world block and press R. The list looks like this:
Craft a Chemical Infuser
Craft an Osmium Compressor

“Infusion” is the mod's invention, but it has an honest prototype: alloying. The additive enters the base metal's lattice, no new compound forms, and the properties change radically. That's how carbon turns iron into steel, and chromium turns it into stainless.
Heat Generator: burns anything hot. The only one that needs nothing from the world.

Not for profit: the “coal → power → electrolysis → hydrogen → power” chain loses energy overall, and there's no cure for that. It's for the form. Gas sits in a tank, flows through tubes and burns where there's no room for a coal furnace. The first energy in the pack that doesn't exist as an item in a slot.
Make 4 Advanced Control Circuits

Cu₈₈Sn₁₂, classic tin bronze: twelve percent tin lowers copper's melting point and doubles its hardness. The Stone Age didn't end with the discovery of copper, it ended with the discovery that copper with something mixed in beats pure copper.

Fifty percent extra on every log. In a world with one tree that you grew by hand, that's not an optimization, it's the difference between “enough” and “not enough”. Planks go into Heat Generators, and as it turned out above, you need a whole row of those.
A ladder with four rungs
So the chambers further up the map aren't built for ore. The Enrichment Chamber is for the eightfold infusion; the Purification and Injection Chambers are for what's behind them in chapter four.

Do the math: that's forty Heat Generators on a single line. You won't hit the basic tier's ceiling in this chapter, and that's fine: the next tiers aren't needed now, they're for when the reactor shows up.
Make 2 Elite Control Circuits
Build a Gas-Burning Generator
&b6&r carbon → &b1&r coal in the Combiner. The rock gives carbon &b14&r%% of the time, second only to iron: the cheapest thing you'll make today.
Metallurgy spent three thousand years doing exactly this. Pure tin is soft and useless, pure nickel is a lab curiosity. Their entire value lies in what they do to someone else's crystal lattice.
Make 2 Basic Chemical Tanks
A network is as good as its worst piece
Make an Advanced Energy Cube

Why this instead of farmland? Farmland needs water within four blocks, and water here exists as a single bucket that can't spread into a pond. Without watering, farmland dries back into dirt in a couple of days. The pot doesn't ask about water at all, or about light either: it grows things in total darkness.
The only hoe in this world
Craft a Rotary Condensentrator
A pot glows with whatever grows in it. Glow berries give light level &b14&r, exactly like a torch, except a torch has to burn carbon, while the berries grow on their own and feed you on the side.

The Induction Matrix is a multiblock of casings with cells and providers placed inside. A cell sets the capacity, a provider sets the speed. A Basic cell stores &b3.2&r billion FE, two thousand times more than a Basic cube.

What stands in its place, you've known since chapter one. The &eDissolver&r takes the rock apart into twelve elements, and the Combiner puts anything back together. That's not second-rate: fivefold processing turns iron ore into five iron ingots, while the Dissolver turns the same block into twelve different elements that anything at all can be made from.

Osmium is the backbone of &6Mekanism&r. The Heat Generator, the Infuser, the basic circuit, the Electrolytic Core, the Gas-Burning Generator: it's in all of them and can't be replaced in any. Thirty-two atoms for two ingots is expensive. It only gets more expensive from here.
Craft an Enrichment Chamber and get 16 Enriched Redstone
The task accepts an osmium ingot from any mod: it checks the forge:ingots/osmium tag. Both &6ChemLib&r and &6Mekanism&r register osmium here, and Almost Unified keeps the one canonical version.
No fire charge here
Up the tiers: Basic has three slots, Advanced five, Elite seven, Ultimate nine. Nine parallel enrichments in one block means a ninth of the space and one cable instead of nine.
Dirt by the recipe
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.02_energy.9: A diamond you don't have to crush
&b4&r osmium ingots, &b2&r casings, &b2&r Infused Alloy and an Electrolytic Core. The fuel is hydrogen from the separator.
Life from powder
A casing, two Advanced Control Circuits, two Infused Alloy and two buckets. The buckets aren't for water here: the compressor doesn't fill them with anything, they're just part of the frame.

Signalum, lumium and enderium simply aren't in this version of Foundation: those items don't exist, and recipes for them won't work no matter how hard you look. Lead exists as an item, but there's no lead in the rock: it arrives with chapter six. Ruby and sapphire exist, but there's deliberately no bridge from elements to them: they don't unlock anything.
C + O₂ → CO₂, about &b33&r MJ per kilogram. The first power in this world is carbon you pulled from under your own feet and set back on fire. The world heats itself by taking itself apart.
&b6&r carbon + &b10&r hydrogen + &b5&r oxygen. Hydrogen is the bottleneck: the rock gives it &b8&r%% of the time, and here you need forty atoms of it.
Mycelium is soil of two categories at once, dirt and mushroom. One block that grows both wheat and mushrooms, so you no longer have to keep two kinds of soil.

Use bone meal on a pot and it gets &b400&r to &b550&r ticks of growth at once. A full cycle is &b1,200&r, so one pinch is roughly a third of a harvest, and the spread isn't there for looks, it's so automation can't be worked out in your head.
Craft an Advanced Tier Installer
&b14&r copper + &b2&r tin. A total of &b16&r: exactly one ingot on the pack's scale.
The hoe isn't needed for anything else here. There's nowhere to till: the only dirt is the dirt you made yourself, and all of it is already in pots.

Poke a pot of dirt with a hoe. The dirt turns into farmland without leaving the pot, and growth speeds up by five percent: &b1,143&r ticks instead of &b1,200&r. And it can't dry out: by definition there's no water in the pot.

2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂. The current tears the molecule apart: hydrogen comes off at the cathode, oxygen at the anode, and there's always twice as much hydrogen by volume, because there's twice as much of it in the formula.
&b3&r iron, &b2&r planks, &b1&r osmium ingot, &b2&r copper and a furnace. Fuel is anything that burns in a furnace; for you, that's coal.

Forty units of refined obsidian infusion per ingot, twice the cost of the diamond rung. The chain is long, but it all runs on machines you already have: obsidian in the Enrichment Chamber gives four Obsidian Dust, the dust in the Infuser with diamond infusion gives Refined Obsidian Dust, that goes back into the chamber to become enriched, and now it carries eighty units.
Make 8 each of Mechanical Pipes, Pressurized Tubes, Logistical Transporters and Thermodynamic Conductors

Look up bronze in JEI and the first thing it shows is a crafting recipe with a Fire Charge in the middle. That's how &6Thermal&r cooks alloys back home. A Fire Charge means blaze powder, blaze powder in &6Alchemistry&r chemistry is made of germanium, and there's no germanium in the rock at all. That road is closed until chapter six, so don't go down it.
&b1&r calcium carbonate + &b1&r iron oxide → redstone.
The Elite cube wants Reinforced Alloy in the corners and gold on the sides, the Ultimate one Atomic Alloy and diamond. Twenty-five million FE and a hundred and two million, respectively.

Output matters more than capacity, and people forget that. A Basic cube stores a million and a half, but gives out &b1&r,&b600&r per tick: that's sixteen Dissolvers and not one more, however much is stored inside.
Stage: energy
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.02_energy.a: The alloy your generator is made of
Craft a Basic Enriching Factory

Sweet berries give the same &b14&r. Both crops sit on plain dirt and both give back more than you planted. In a pack where lighting is paid for with rock, a row of pots along the wall isn't decoration.
The first thing that stores energy
Craft an Energized Smelter

This is the only machine in the pack that guzzles water by the bucket, and it stands in a world without a single drop. Every bucket comes from hydrogen, and the rock is eight percent hydrogen. The plant works; just remember what every turn of it costs you.
2 · Energy
Iron ingot into the Infuser, redstone into the infusion tank. Ten units per ingot, so one redstone per alloy.
Craft a Precision Sawmill
Make 2 Energy Tablets
&b100&r SO₂ and &b50&r oxygen in the Chemical Infuser: &b100&r SO₃;
Make 8 Enriched Carbon and 2 Enriched Tin
Grow 16 wheat in a pot
The whole table on one circuit

Another road works, and it's shorter. The Enrichment Chamber turns a whole diamond into an Enriched Diamond, and anything enriched always gives eighty units of infusion instead of ten. Twenty units per alloy, so one little stone is four Reinforced Alloy.
Make 4 Dirt blocks
Funny thing: both roads cost the same. The Combiner and the dusts both come out to exactly sixteen atoms per ingot. Two machines from different mods landed on the same number without any collusion.
Eighty versus two hundred
The glue of all Mekanism
&6Mekanism&r Generators offers six power sources. Let's go down the list.
Make 2 Refined Obsidian Ingots
Make 4 Induction Casings
A pot that harvests itself
Until now it was a matter of faith
Make one ingot each of tin, nickel and silver
Power, at last
A diamond and a half per circuit
Machines don't run on enthusiasm
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.02_energy.b: &b1&r kaolinite + &b1&r cellulose + &b1&r water → dirt.
The real storage in this mod is something else, and it's the next quest.
The tablet is a portable battery and a required part of the Energy Cube, the Configurator and the Resistive Heater. The first thing in the pack that stores energy instead of spending it.
Notice what this branch never had once: a wire. While the rest of the workshop counts FE per tick, ten pots run with no power at all.

And this chapter needs five more that aren't on the list either. Osmium: not a single &6Mekanism&r machine can be built without it. Strontium: the rock holds six tenths of a percent, and redstone eats it by the stack. Tin, nickel and silver: without them there isn't a single alloy.
Make 4 Electrum Ingots
&b20&r FE/t and no fuel. With this machine, an expense that has dragged on since chapter one disappears: smelting no longer costs sixteen carbon atoms a pop.

This stage gates the &eAtomizer&r, the &eLiquifier&r and the Industrial tiers of &6Alchemistry&r machines. It's easy to tell if this is your case: the quest is complete, the reward is claimed, and these items still drop out of your inventory and can't be picked up from the ground. That means the grant command didn't fire.
Nickel is one of the five elements that aren't in the rock. Every invar ingot costs six atoms taken from who knows where.

2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, &b286&r kJ per mole: the highest heat of combustion per kilogram of anything humanity has tried burning. The combustion product is water. In a world without water, the cleanest way to get energy gives back exactly the water the separator took apart a moment ago.
A pot plus a hopper. This pot harvests by itself and pushes the crop down into whatever container sits right below it. No redstone, no power, no timer.
No garden beds here
Gas-Burning: burns hydrogen, hydrogen comes from electrolysis, and electrolysis costs more than the burning gives back. Useful, but not as a source. That branch is further down the map.

The water in these recipes is the compound chemlib:water, two hydrogens and an oxygen, not a bucket. There isn't a drop of liquid water in the world: you can place the bucket from the starter chest and scoop it back up as often as you like, but a single source can't spread into a pond.
Two tanks in, one out. The machine knows exactly three reactions, and all three are real.

Break the deepslate with a pickaxe and it drops cobbled deepslate, which is in the minecraft:stone_crafting_materials tag. That gives you the furnace, stone tools and everything that used to need cobblestone. Without this recipe there's nowhere to get a furnace, and the chapter ends at step one.
Perpetual motion, attempt two

From here, everything the mod calls “ultimate” stands on Atomic Alloy: the Ultimate Control Circuit, the Ultimate Energy Cube, the Ultimate Universal Cable, the Teleporter. This is the last rung a chapter about electricity can reach at all.

The rock is three percent sulfur, sixteen atoms per dust: the most accessible raw material for the gas line. This is where the second half of the chapter begins: until now the only gases were hydrogen and oxygen from the separator, and now there are many.
From here on it gets into everything: the Energy Tablet, the Electrolytic Core, the separator, the Gas-Burning Generator, two to five of them each.
It burns into water
Get 4 Mycelium blocks
Set up the faces with the Configurator. In &6Mekanism&r input and output are set per side of the block, and a cube with every face set to input will dutifully store energy and never give any out.
The last one is the least obvious: it carries not energy but temperature. You'll need it when you want to burn fuel in one place and draw power in another.
Time to do the math. &6Mekanism&r thinks in joules, displays FE, and its exchange rate is &b2.5&r joules per FE.
You already have oxygen: the separator pumps it out alongside the hydrogen, and until now half its output went nowhere. From this point on, oxygen stops being waste.

The Configurator takes a stick, lapis lazuli, a tablet and &b2&r alloy. You have a stick: the tree grew. Lapis is made in the Combiner: &b3&r silicon + &b6&r sodium + &b3&r mullite + &b2&r calcium sulfide, all from the rock.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.02_energy.c: An Advanced Control Circuit between two Reinforced Alloy. Nothing new except the price: every Elite Control Circuit carries a basic circuit, two Infused Alloy and two Reinforced Alloy, and that's already a diamond and a half.

And the Heat Generator turns heat back into energy through the Seebeck effect, and here the efficiency is far from perfect. Put one next to the other and you get a machine that reliably reduces the amount of energy in the system. Perpetual motion, attempt two, with the same result as the first.

Inside is the Seebeck effect, discovered in &b1821&r: a temperature difference across the junction of two conductors produces a voltage. No moving parts, lousy efficiency, but it runs on anything hot. It can also draw heat from adjacent lava, but there's no lava here.

When short on power, &6Alchemistry&r machines don't run slower: they just sit there and charge up. Hover over the Dissolver: the tooltip says how many FE/t it needs. That's a minimum, not a wish, so plan for about ten percent on top.
Burn 16 charcoal

If you've played &6Mekanism&r before, you're looking for the ore processing line right now. The Enrichment Chamber gives two ingots instead of one, the Purification Chamber three, the Injection Chamber four, the Dissolution Chamber with the Crystallizer five. That's the heart of the mod and the reason it gets put into modpacks.
Gold is the rarest element in the rock, &b1&r%%. Three ingots are &b48&r atoms, which is about five thousand dissolved blocks. Don't be surprised by the math.
In &6Mekanism&r terms, oxidizing means turning a solid into a gas. A sulfur dust gives &b100&r mB of sulfur dioxide, a salt gives &b15&r mB of brine, a lithium dust gives &b100&r mB of lithium.
&7You got through the first chapter by hand&r: you took the rock under your feet apart into twelve elements and made your first things out of them.
Make an Elite Energy Cube

Nine copper and seven nickel, Cu₅₅Ni₄₅. The name comes from constancy: this alloy's resistivity barely depends on temperature, which is why it's used for reference resistors and, most importantly, thermocouples.

Tin makes for especially pleasant math. Three copper ingots and ten units of tin give four bronze in the Infuser, and an enriched dust carries eighty units, so that's thirty-two bronze from a single dust. Carbon goes into &6Mekanism&r steel: an iron ingot and ten units give Enriched Iron, ten more give Steel Dust.
&8The purity isn't ninety-nine point one percent, of course. But for chapter two it'll do.&r

The rock is a quarter of a percent osmium: one ingot takes &b6,400&r dissolved blocks. On the starter furnace-and-generator setup that ingot takes over four hours, and &6Mekanism&r asks for them by the dozen.

A thermocouple is a junction of two different conductors that produces a voltage from a temperature difference. The most common pair, type T, is copper and constantan. So the Heat Generator that the whole chapter rests on is built, inside, from exactly what you just made. The mod says nothing about it, but the coincidence is real.
And it comes as a factory too: three slots, then five, then seven, then nine.

The Advanced Control Circuit isn't decoration. The Purification Chamber, the Osmium Compressor, the evaporation plant and the second-tier factory all stand on it. It'll be asked for constantly until the end of the chapter, so make four right away.
Build an Electrolytic Separator and split water into hydrogen and oxygen
Build an Enricher and get 4 Trace Concentrate
Five items carry five different things, yet they're crafted the same way: two strips of steel and something in the middle.
A service quest. It's for one case only: the “energy” stage was supposed to come as a reward but didn't.
&b1&r aluminum + &b1&r iron + &b1&r silicon dioxide. Three components, none of them rare: the cheapest stone in the pack and, more importantly, the only one.
Read why, in a pack with six generators, you're burning coal
A casing, &b2&r circuits, &b2&r iron, &b4&r Infused Alloy. There's no redstone in the recipe; it goes into the finished machine.
A cactus on eight silicon dioxide
This is where the chemistry ends. A living organism can't be assembled from two handfuls of polymer and a gulp of oxygen, not in reality and not in theory. Everything else in this chapter is real.
The casing is the shared base of every &6Mekanism&r machine. The Enrichment Chamber, the Energized Smelter, the Energy Cube, the Gas-Burning Generator: all of them are a casing plus the insides.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.02_energy.d: The Ultimate Energy Cube, the Ultimate Universal Cable and the Ultimate Tier Installer all stand on it. You'll meet all of them below, but no recipe in this chapter will ever ask for anything more expensive.

Of all the infusion types in the mod, this is the only one that runs on something that grows. Redstone needs strontium, diamond needs five hundred and twelve carbon atoms, tin and gold need metals from the tail of the table. Fungi comes from a pot of deepslate and costs nothing.

The main thing to know about &6Mekanism&r cable: it has no losses. Not over length, not on bends, not by the number of receivers. There's exactly one limit, how much FE passes per tick, and the basic cable handles &b3&r,&b200&r.

Eight silicon dioxide make a block of sand. The cheapest soil you can print, and exactly one crop grows on it: cactus. Sugar cane and bamboo want sand too, but there's nothing to make them from: no Combiner recipe exists for them.
Real deepslate is feldspars, quartz, mica and a bit of iron. &6Alchemistry&r squeezes that down to three ingredients. Crude, but elementally it's in the right ballpark.
Grow 32 potatoes
Wind Generator: output grows with height, and there's nothing to build a tower from except the very rock you're dissolving into elements. Also removed.
Kaolinite, Al₂Si₂O₅(OH)₄, is ordinary white clay, the stuff porcelain is made from. Dirt according to &6Alchemistry&r is clay, humus and moisture. For soil, that description is surprisingly honest.
The mushroom that makes soil

Sulfuric acid is called the index of industry for good reason: for decades its annual output was used as a measure of a country's development, because it goes into almost everything (fertilizers, metals, fuels, explosives, batteries). Here it will unlock hydrofluoric acid, uranium hexafluoride and half of chapter eight.
Half of Thermal didn't make it here

It has exactly the same four tiers, and they differ by exactly the same circuits and alloys. By this point in the chapter the tier circuit stops being just an ingredient and becomes a unit of measurement: say “elite”, and whoever you're talking to understands the price, the speed and the throughput.
Glass, Infused Alloy and a dust in the middle. Osmium dust gives the Speed Upgrade, gold the Energy Upgrade, tin the Filter Upgrade, iron the Gas Upgrade, steel the Muffling Upgrade.

The rock's main list ends at gold, but the Dissolver doesn't. Below it comes a tail that's easy to scroll past in the tooltip: magnesium &b2&r, potassium &b1.6&r, phosphorus &b1.2&r, titanium &b1&r, chlorine &b0.8&r, manganese &b0.7&r, strontium &b0.6&r, zinc &b0.5&r, tin &b0.4&r, nickel &b0.3&r, osmium &b0.25&r, silver &b0.15&r, platinum &b0.1&r.
Make 16 Basic Universal Cables
A farm that makes its own soil
Twelve out of a hundred and eighteen
The Resistive Heater turns energy into heat with perfect efficiency: as much FE as goes in, that much heat comes out. No heater in the world does better; that's what makes it a resistor.

The real-world analogue is steel again: iron with an additive driven into its lattice, so the layers stop sliding over each other. What redstone is doing in there, the mod doesn't explain. And it's right not to.
Eight to one, always
Redstone: Universal Cable, energy. A bucket: Mechanical Pipe, liquids. Glass: Pressurized Tube, gases. A circuit: Logistical Transporter, items. Copper: Thermodynamic Conductor, heat.
Four steps in the Combiner:
The two reddest substances

From the side it can be read by a comparator: the signal grows along with the plant and hits the ceiling when it's ready to harvest. If you want a row of pots feeding one belt, this is where to start.
Make 8 Bronze Ingots
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.02_energy.e: Hydrogen and chlorine give hydrogen chloride. Oxygen and two sulfur dioxide give two sulfur trioxide. Sulfur trioxide and water vapor give sulfuric acid.

Real electronics don't use osmium: its tetroxide, OsO₄, is volatile and highly toxic, and nobody would work with it on a factory floor. Osmium-iridium alloys, though, go into electrical contacts and the bearings of precision instruments: they practically don't wear. The “osmium circuit board” is made up; the “osmium in the contacts” isn't.
Make a Basic Energy Cube
Wood pays off twice
Grow 16 cacti
Craft a Hopper Botany Pot and put a chest under it
Two slots: soil on the left, seeds on the right. You can already make dirt: kaolinite, cellulose and water. The Combiner makes wheat seeds from sucrose and triglyceride.
Make 2 Atomic Alloy
Collect 16 atoms each of tin, nickel and silver
&b1&r calcium + &b1&r carbonate → calcium carbonate;

Fe₂O₃ is hematite, a.k.a. plain rust: it's what colors both rust and Martian soil. Stock &6Alchemistry&r paired it with strontium carbonate (strontium salts give fireworks their crimson flame), but the rock only gives six tenths of a percent strontium, and you'd never make enough redstone on that. Calcium took its place: the same class of compound, it just burns orange. The substitution was forced, and it's better to know about it up front.
Read why Mekanism's main mechanic doesn't work here
Output matters more than capacity

And mushrooms grow on mulch. So the wheat pot makes soil for the mushroom pot, the mushroom pot feeds the Infuser, and the whole branch stops depending on the Dissolver. The first closed-loop production in the pack where nothing comes from the rock.

The separator isn't a source, it's a converter: it spends more than the Gas-Burning Generator will give back. The “water → hydrogen → energy → water” loop crashes into the first law of thermodynamics, and it has crashed for everyone who's ever tried it.
Make 4 Reinforced Alloy
&b2&r cellulose + &b1&r oxygen. Pick any species: oak, birch, spruce, acacia, jungle, dark oak; they all have the same composition.
Build 4 Heat Generators

There's no water in this world. There's a recipe for water: sixteen molecules per bucket, each made of two hydrogens and an oxygen. The matrix is doable, but it's not a project for today, and you need the casing right now precisely so you don't build it blind.
Bio-Generator: runs on Bio Fuel, Bio Fuel comes from the Crusher, and the Crusher wants a bucket of lava. No lava, no branch, the whole thing gone.

Speed and Energy pull in opposite directions, and you need to understand that before you stuff a machine full of upgrades. Speed makes operations faster and at the same time raises consumption. Energy lowers consumption. Eight slots per machine, and the best layout is almost always a mix.
&b2&r silicon dioxide + &b1&r aluminum oxide + &b2&r water → kaolinite;
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.02_energy.f: Infused Alloy into the Infuser, diamond into the tank. Just not the diamond itself: the Infuser accepts diamond dust, dust comes from the Crusher, and the Crusher needs two buckets of lava. There's no lava.

Is a hundred million a lot or a little? The &eDissolver&r eats &b5&r,&b000&r FE per operation. So the Ultimate cube holds twenty thousand dissolutions, roughly a day of work for a decent workshop. As an emergency reserve, great. As the basis of your power grid, no: a cube doesn't produce anything.
It burns coal, and coal is six carbon atoms. Everything you smelt is paid for with rock. Later the Energized Smelter will come along and remove that cost for good.

The generator puts out a steady trickle, but &6Alchemistry&r machines eat in bursts: the Dissolver charges up to a threshold, fires, charges again. Without a buffer, half the time goes to waiting. The cube smooths out the peaks and also shows you, as a number, how much energy you actually have.
Easier to assemble than to forge
The first engineered material

The common denominator: a generator draws energy from a difference in temperature, pressure, light or concentration. A dead flat plane has no differences. The only one you can create here, you create yourself, by setting carbon on fire.
&aThis quest unlocks the “Steel” and “Twilight Forest” chapters.&r
Perpetual motion, attempt one
Without it, gas never leaves the system at all: you can't fill a bucket with it, put it in a chest, or hand it to another mod. Everything you brew on the gas line has to be condensed here first.
A planted sapling returns more planks than it cost. The first renewable resource in the whole pack, and the only thing here that grows by itself.
Fill a bucket with sulfuric acid

The Elite Control Circuit unlocks the Chemical Injection Chamber, the Chemical Dissolution Chamber, the Chemical Crystallizer and the Induction Port. Half of that is useless in a world without ores, and the other half is the gas line at the end of the chapter.
One frame, five fillings
A bone is three hydroxylapatite, Ca₅(PO₄)₃OH. That's literally the mineral part of real bone, so the recipe is honest down to the formula. One bone, three bone meal.

The alloy branch is optional. Of &6Thermal&r, only Foundation was kept here (materials without machines), and bronze, invar and electrum are needed to fill the forge:ingots/* tags that other mods' recipes ask for.
Start the chapter
The ingot itself goes into the Teleporter, the Ultimate Energy Cube and Atomic Alloy. The Teleporter is a long way off, but the alloy is needed two quests from now.
Make 8 Infused Alloy

Pour water straight into the machine with a bucket, right click. Two buckets in a two-by-two pit make an infinite source: the vanilla mechanic works here, and the second bucket from chapter one finally comes in handy.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.01: Build a Seared Channel and split casting across several tables
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.02: Five bricks and a gauge. The Melter goes directly on top of the Seared Heater, otherwise there's nothing to heat it.
A pickaxe is a head, a handle and a binding. Copper is the easiest place to start: the Part Builder cuts it. Once the smeltery is running, the heads will be cast from steel.
Both kinds keep their contents when broken. You can carry a tank of lava in your pocket: until you have pipes, it's the only way at all to move more than a bucket of lava at a time.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.03: Other mods' recipes will take it
