Put a Pattern above any crafting table and the table becomes a Crafting Station. That's it, that's the whole recipe.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.05: The smeltery opens up alloys the Combiner doesn't make. Bronze: three copper to one tin. Invar: two iron to one nickel. Constantan: one copper to one nickel. Electrum: one gold to one silver.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.06: Read and understand why things get awkward from here
Stone part cast over with clay
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.07: Got it: material first, then levels

Three silicon dioxide in the press make a piece of flint. The same flint through the &eCombiner&r costs six: twice the price for the same thing. That's what happens when two machines can do the same job and a different person did the math for each.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.08: The quest is completed with a checkmark, not an item, and that's not laziness. &6Tinkers&r keeps the material in NBT: the same pickaxe with a copper head and with a steel head is two different sets of data under one item ID. An item task would count either nothing or anything at all.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.09: &6Tinkers&r tanks come in two capacities, and the difference isn't random. The fuel tank holds &b4000&r mB, exactly four buckets. The ingot tank holds &b4320&r, exactly forty-eight ingots. One counts in buckets, the other in metal, and each is a round number in its own unit.

Heating them isn't hard: bronze &b700&r, electrum &b760&r, invar and constantan a little over nine hundred each; lava takes all of them with room to spare. Just don't count on alloying bronze on coal because the heater reaches seven hundred degrees: the smeltery doesn't understand solid fuel at all, it needs a tank of liquid. Coal here feeds the melter, and the melter doesn't alloy.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.0a: Four carbon make graphite, eight graphite make a pinch of graphite dust, sixteen pinches make a diamond. Multiply it out: five hundred and twelve carbon atoms for one little rock. A Steel Ingot costs one.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.0e: Hence a simple rule: the head is picked for tier and durability, the handle for whatever the head lacks. The same metal in all three parts is almost always worse than a mix.

Take the spectrum of the &eWhite Antimatter&r under your feet. It is &b0.25&r%% osmium, and at the very bottom sits platinum, &b1&r in &b1000&r operations. That's why the &eEnricher&r showed up in chapter two.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.11: &aThis quest unlocks the chapters “Industry”, “Compounds”, “Settlement”, “Create”, “Ars Nouveau”, “Apotheosis” and “Contracts”.&r
The melter holds one metal and one recipe at a time: drop in a copper ingot and you get &b90&r mB of molten metal, which piles up in the tank ingot by ingot. Only a faucet can get it out.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.12: Notice: sand, gravel and stone are all the same silicon dioxide. The difference between a grain of sand, a pebble and a cliff isn't chemical but geological, a matter of how many million years water has spent grinding them down. The press doesn't have millions of years, so it makes up the difference with quantity.

Every part swap cuts the accumulated experience in half. It doesn't wipe it, it halves it, but two or three upgrades in a row knock the tool back a level, and that's exactly what you'll feel like doing the day steel finally starts flowing.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.13: A cast you never have to make again

Obsidian is frozen lava. Volcanic glass: the melt cooled so fast that crystals had no time to grow, and the rock set as glass instead of stone. Melting obsidian back into lava isn't something the mod made up, it's literally undoing that quench.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.15: “Silky”: five Silky Cloth, blocks drop as themselves. “Lucky”: copper, lapis and a flower, with two more levels after that. “Autosmelt”: everything drops already smelted. “Expanded”: a wider reach. “Exchanging”, “Pathing”, “Stripping”: about convenience, not yield.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.16: Put 4 Seared Glass into the smeltery wall. Optional

In JEI the machine is called Melting Chamber, ID cyclic:melter. Two redstone blocks, quartz, two glass, a furnace and three obsidian; all of it can already be made from elements. The lava recipe: stone plus obsidian → &b1000&r mB for &b16&r,&b000&r FE.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.18: You'll need diamonds for the second &eCombiner&r, then for &6Tinkers&r modifiers, then for all of chapter four. Get the press running nonstop ahead of time instead of waiting until you're desperate.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.19: Hence the early-game rule: cast the heavy parts from whatever you have plenty of, and save expensive alloys for heads. The head decides tier and durability; everything else is fine-tuning.
Three seared blocks on top and four stone as legs. The table doesn't apply modifiers: it works on them.

A reinforcement is cast on the casting table: a blank Pattern underneath, molten metal on top, and the Pattern is used up along with the metal. Iron costs &b90&r mB of iron, gold the same amount of gold, seared &b250&r mB of molten stone, obsidian a whole 1000 mB.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.1c: One rate for everything: eight molecule items one way, &b500&r mB the other. The Liquifier's and the &eAtomizer&r's lists match line for line: thirty-nine entries, and everything that can be poured out can be collected back.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.1d: And it isn't the only one. Vine has a trait that feeds on sunlight, and there's no sky over this world at all. &6Tinkers&r materials came from a world that never happened here, and some of their strengths stayed behind.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.20: The melter can do exactly one thing: turn an item into its own molten form. Two liquids will never meet in it: there's one tank and one liquid at a time, and it simply won't accept a second.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.21: A pickaxe gets one ability, the contenders are many, and they're all mutually exclusive.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.24: Here's the point. A faucet pours one portion per click, and you have twenty casts. A channel turns one click into twenty castings, and a redstone signal into a conveyor that keeps running while you're busy with something else.
Build a tool with the handle and the head made of different materials
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.25: Build a Spectrometer and take the spectrum of the rock
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.26: Then the smeltery: &b90&r mB of copper and &b100&r mB of molten amethyst give &b90&r mB of alloy. All the amethyst volume vanishes into nothing: you pay with two, you get one. And amethyst melts at &b950&r, so you can't touch it without lava.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.27: Flint isn't just for the flint and steel to light the portal. It's also a tier-one &6Tinkers&r material: a flint head has less durability than a stone one, but hits noticeably harder. If neighboring chapters said there's no flint in this world, they meant the time before the press.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.28: Build a Seared Heater: 8 Seared Bricks in a ring
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.2c: There's also the Scorched Alloyer, which alloys without any multiblock, as a single block. It's made of scorched stone, and that only comes from the Nether.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.2f: The simplest alloy in the mod: &b90&r mB of copper plus &b90&r mB of gold make &b180&r. Nothing is lost, and it melts at &b550&r: a coal heater could handle it, if only it could alloy.
Cut a Large Plate, the most expensive part the Part Builder makes
Steel takes one atom per ingot. The rest is fuel: &b4&r carbon make graphite, &b2&r graphite make coal, and that coal will later fire up &6Tinkers&r.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.30: Take sand casts of a Pick Head and a Tool Handle

The sponge in this world doesn't come from the ocean. The &eCombiner&r makes it from kaolinite and chalk, and the wet one from the same plus sixteen waters. A nice little touch: a mechanic designed around ocean monuments runs on chemistry here.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.31: Hold Alt to see the points in the tooltip. The mod has its own level names: first “Like New”, then “Clumsy”, and on up to “Transcendent”, which nobody I know of has ever reached.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.32: Make 64 sand, 64 gravel and 32 clay balls
The difference is what happens next. A sand cast goes away with the casting: one pour, one cast. A gold one survives any number of pours, and in mass production that's the only thing that matters.

The smeltery is a sealed box, and on its own it won't let anything in or out. Two blocks fix that: the Seared Drain passes liquids, the Seared Chute passes items. Both go right into the wall in place of a regular brick and work both ways.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.34: A pickaxe that won't run out
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.35: For a long time only metals got that luxury. Silicon, boron, germanium, arsenic, antimony and tellurium are metalloids, and the recipe generator didn't count them as metals: the dust items exist in the game, the tag exists, but there was no way to get them at all. Here all six got the same rate, sixteen to one.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.36: The spirit they blamed for poisonings

Seared Fuel Tank: &b8&r bricks and glass in the center. The tank goes under the smeltery floor and is filled with lava; one bucket lasts a long time. The smeltery itself: walls and floor of Seared Bricks, the controller in a wall, a drain to the outside, at least &b3×3&r inside.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.37: There's no other way to get steel into Tinkers: the Part Builder won't cut it. Metals in &6Tinkers&r exist only through melting.

This stage gates the ME Controller, the Molecular Assembler and the Pattern Provider. It's easy to tell if this is your case: the quest is completed, the reward claimed, but these items still pop out of your inventory and can't be picked up off the ground. That means the grant command didn't fire.
And don't confuse it with the glass pane that looks just like it. The pane doesn't fit into the multiblock at all, even though it looks like it belongs there.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.39: Iron, pistons, redstone and two stone pressure plates. No steel needed: build it right now, the left half of the chapter won't start without it.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.3d: Clay, sand and gravel on a crafting table give two Grout; Grout in a furnace becomes a brick. The raw materials are already there from the previous quest.
Work out what each new layer costs
Run water full circle: Combiner → Liquifier → Atomizer
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.3e: There are also gold casts, and they last longer. But gold has to be assembled from atoms first, while sand you have by the &eCompactor&r-load.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.41: Dissolve the rock: it is &b14&r%% carbon, second only to iron. Coal goes into the &eDissolver&r too, but feeding it what it just spat out is an acquired taste.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.42: &b96&r covers the heater, melter, faucet, table, basin and smeltery controller with a little to spare. A &b3×3&r smeltery will eat as many again, so better keep the furnace lit.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.43: Check how many slots a finished tool has
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.44: Gauges are the same tanks with a glass side: same capacity, but you can see the level. They go into the smeltery wall just like the solid ones, and a fuel gauge fully replaces a fuel tank.

Pig Iron will never happen. The recipe asks for Meat Soup, and in this mod Meat Soup comes exactly one way: a living animal falls into a running smeltery. There are no animals here. It's the only &6Tinkers&r alloy locked away in this world forever, and what locks it isn't rare ore, it's that there's simply nobody to cook it from.
Find out what extra upgrades cost. Optional branch
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.45: Binding picked for its trait, not its numbers
Understand why only digging tools grow
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.48: Learn what an upgrade costs before swapping a part
Pick the one ability for your first pickaxe
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.49: Got it: there is no depth here
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.4a: Look at what they're really made of. The rock is four tenths of a percent tin, three tenths nickel, fifteen hundredths silver. Copper and gold come in more or less by themselves, but the alloying addition means thousands of dissolved blocks for a handful of atoms. That's why additions are taken from the Enricher's Trace Concentrate, not from the rock. Real life works exactly the same way: an alloy always costs more than its base metal, and it's the addition that makes it cost more.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.4b: Amethyst in the Combiner is one iron atom and one silicon dioxide. That's not made up: amethyst really is quartz whose color an iron impurity plus natural irradiation have turned purple. Take away the iron and you're left with plain rock crystal.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.4d: The half percent in every alloy

A hundred and fifty degrees, and nothing to close the gap with. Coal doesn't get hotter because there's more of it: &b800&r isn't “not enough fuel”, it's the ceiling of the fuel. Pile the heater to the brim if you like.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.4e: Five hundred and twelve atoms per rock
Get a tool to level three

There's no lava in the world: no lakes, no Nether. The Nether is still two chapters away, and its portal is made of the same obsidian. So here lava isn't found, it's cooked: from stone that didn't exist and from glass you quenched yourself. Probably the most telling recipe in the chapter: the world didn't give you a single link of this chain.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.4f: German miners gave it its name. The ore glittered like silver, yielded no silver, and poisoned the smelters with arsenic when roasted, so the blame fell on the kobold, a mountain spirit. Arsenic, by the way, now gets pressed into dust here too, and poisons nobody.
With steel the loop opens up fair and square: this Dissolver is built from what a Dissolver itself mined. No more gifts.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.50: In real life you break it
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.51: Click the checkmark and claim the reward: the stage will be granted again. If you already have it, nothing changes: granting it twice is harmless.

Right-click a block and its spectrum appears in chat: every Dissolver group with its chance, plus the rarest drop on a separate line, “chance per operation 1 in so-many”. Click machines with &eShift&r held, or their window opens instead. You can also hold a sample in your offhand and click the air.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.52: The binding doesn't change a single number

That's not why you take it. The “Enhanced” trait gives the tool an extra upgrade slot, one slot for each part. So rose gold is the only slot boost in the chapter that takes nothing in return. Put it in the binding: it costs one ingot, gives no numbers anyway, and brings the whole trait.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.55: The reverse of the &eAtomizer&r: item in, fluid out. A &6ChemLib&r compound becomes its own liquid: water, ammonia, acids, gases. You need it wherever chemistry carries on into other mods: they only understand fluids and want nothing to do with molecule items.

You won't need this tomorrow, but in chapter eight, where compounds become the content. Still, it's worth knowing now which pair of machines they pour out of: then you won't have to rearrange your workshop.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.56: Now add up what you got. An amethyst bronze head: &b720&r durability, speed &b7&r, diamond tier. A steel one: &b775&r and speed &b6&r. A Steel Ingot costs sixteen iron atoms, while an ingot of this alloy costs a copper ingot, one iron atom and one silica. The best tool in the chapter is made almost from scrap, and it's called bronze even though there isn't a gram of tin in it.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.59: Now throw in Steel Ingots. Lava gives &b1000&r, steel needs &b950&r: fifty degrees to spare, and the gap is closed.

The ingot is Mekanism's, but we're the ones who put it into the &eCombiner&r. The mod itself would hand it to you two tiers later, via the infuser, Enriched Iron and osmium. Here it is assembled straight from atoms, and the item is exactly the same one you'd get the native way.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.5b: Put it right next to the Part Builder and the Tinker Station: it picks up neighboring stations as tabs too, and you won't have to carry parts around by hand anymore.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.5c: Sand casting is the oldest casting method there is, and it works exactly the same way: press the model in, pull it out, pour metal into the impression. And the mold gets used up honestly, like a real one: it's broken to get the casting out. Want a reusable one? Cast it in gold.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.5f: All made of Seared Bricks. The faucet hangs on the side of the melter, a table or basin goes under the faucet, right-click, and the metal flows down. The table casts small things: ingots, tool parts, casts. The basin casts big things: blocks and the smeltery controller.
Iron, a diamond, obsidian, a piston and steel in the center. The diamond comes from the &eCompactor&r out of carbon, the obsidian from the &eCombiner&r.

What it can do: remove a modifier and give the slot back, reorder modifiers with a compass, hide extra lines from the tooltip. It removes them with a wet sponge, and the sponge comes back dry, but everything that went into the removed modifier vanishes without a trace.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.60: A &b3&r by &b3&r smeltery two layers tall burns three times as much as a melter. Lava burns at &b50&r mB per hundred ticks and the tank holds four buckets, so under constant melting a full tank is gone in a matter of minutes. A melter on the same lava lasts three times longer; it just melts one item at a time.

Every part has its own material cost, and the spread is eightfold. Tool Handle: one ingot. Tool Binding: one. Pick Head: two. Tough Handle: three. Large Plate: four. Hammer Head and Broad Blade: eight each.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.61: Build a Melting Chamber and get a bucket of lava
Got it: cobalt is chapter six
A service quest. It's for one case only: the “steel” stage should have come as a reward, but didn't.
Read it and don't search in vain
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.63: Upgrades and abilities are separate shelves, and one doesn't spill over into the other. Most tools get exactly one ability for their whole life, and choosing it is the most expensive decision you'll make about the tool.
Cut stone and flint heads and compare them at the station
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.64: Don't look for the Tool Forge
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.65: Once you have lots of casts, build a Cast Chest: Seared Bricks around a wooden chest and a gold cast on top. It holds only casts, but all of them, with search by name.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.66: Water has three states here, and they aren't interchangeable: a molecule item for the &eCombiner&r, a fluid for pipes and boilers, a bucket for you. This pair of machines is the adapter between the first two. Without them, chemistry and plumbing live in different universes.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.6a: Now look around. One layer of rock under your feet and emptiness in every direction. No mine, no depth, no height: the only way to dig here is sideways. The trait that carries copper through the whole early mine in a normal game does absolutely nothing here.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.6b: The faucet doesn't pull anything by itself. It opens on a click or a redstone signal and pours exactly one portion: casting automation here is built on redstone, not on pipes.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.6e: You're already pressing diamonds. An emerald in the Combiner is beryl, chromium and vanadium, and the rock gives none of the three. You'll have to hold out until chapter six for emeralds.

Don't look at the table. Stone has the “Stonebound” trait: the more worn down it is, the faster it digs and the weaker it hits. Flint's “Jagged” is the mirror image: it gets dull and meaner for it. Both scale with the share of durability lost, so a brand-new tool gets neither.
You can't get here too early: the fix only unlocks after the quest that grants the stage in the first place.
Get a tool to level one
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.72: The anvil makes the heavy tools (the Sledge Hammer, the Excavator, the Cleaver) and lifts the station's limit on modifiers. For clearing rock, the hammer is irreplaceable: it digs &b3×3&r.
An impression can be taken from anything that has one: Pick Head, Tool Handle, Tool Binding, Tough Handle, Large Plate, Maille, nugget, gear, coin, Repair Kit. Close to thirty entries in all.

Three alloy blocks on top, four seared blocks below. The #tconstruct:anvil_metal tag accepts bronze, &ebrass&r, invar, electrum, constantan, signalum, lumium and enderium: exactly the alloys the &eCombiner&r has been making since chapter two. Plain steel isn't in the tag: the anvil needs an actual alloy.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.73: What you get: &b225&r durability, speed &b6.5&r, iron tier. Faster than an iron head, and faster than a steel one. The price: a stone part and half a clay ball.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.74: Got it: alloys only in the smeltery
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.76: Each one leads to its own armor protection, five per level: iron guards against arrows, gold against magic, seared against fire, obsidian against explosions, cobalt against melee. All five together combine into general “Protection”, and that's an ability, not an upgrade.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.77: It goes under the melter and burns ordinary solid fuel. You have coal: &b4&r carbon make graphite, &b2&r graphite make coal.
One gold ingot per cast, but it's forever. With sand, the same work needs a cast for every pour, and every time it has to be taken again, and every time by hand.
Alloy and cast 4 Amethyst Bronze Ingots
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.78: Open any material at the station and look at the binding line. It's empty. The same for all of the mod's eighty-plus materials: no durability, no damage, no speed. The binding doesn't move a single number.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.79: Trace the whole chain: white rock → iron and carbon → &eCombiner&r → steel → tag → melter → &b950&r °C → molten metal → tool part. You didn't find a single link. You built every one of them.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.7a: It all comes from two compounds. SiO₂ is silicon and two oxygens. Kaolinite, the very clay porcelain is made from, is &b2&r SiO₂, alumina and &b2&r water. Then the &eCompactor&r: &b4&r SiO₂ make sand, &b1&r makes gravel, &b1&r makes stone, &b3&r make flint; kaolinite turns into clay one for one.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.7b: A pickaxe's table has four entries. “Reinforced” and “Haste” weigh five each, “Experienced” three, “Magnetic” two: so durability and speed come up four times as often as the magnet. Each one caps at level five. The sword's table has eleven entries, armor three or four, the Excavator and the Scythe only two.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.7c: The rock is &b18&r%% iron, more than anything else. The world is set up so that iron is always there and everything else has to be waited for.
Handle not picked to match the head
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.7e: Armor counts its own way: plate armor has two upgrades and three defense slots and no abilities at all. The slimesuit, on the other hand, has five upgrades, and that's exactly why people love it.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.7f: Levels by themselves give nothing. Multiples of three do: at the third, sixth and ninth, the tool draws a random modifier from its table.
A table that takes things back
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.80: Remember this number: &b800&r °C. That's what solid fuel gives, and it's a ceiling, not a dial: more coal doesn't mean hotter. Copper melts at &b500&r, gold at &b700&r, iron at exactly &b800&r. The melter will take all of these.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.81: From here on it doesn't matter whose machine made it. Reactor Casing, &6NuclearCraft&r machines, the TConstruct smeltery: they all look at the tag, not at the maker's stamp.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.82: Five Seared Bricks in a U shape give five channels. A channel takes whatever the faucet pours from above and spreads it to the sides: to four at once, or chained into the next channel. Sides are toggled by clicking the face you want.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.85: Build a Faucet, a Casting Table and a Casting Basin

And it multiplies both ways. Copper: plus ten to speed, minus twenty to durability. Bone: minus twenty-five to durability for plus ten to attack speed. Rose gold: plus ten to speed and minus thirty to durability, a third of the tool's life for a tenth more pace.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.86: &8Purity starts with analysis. Heisenberg would approve.&r
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.88: For the record: in real life it's the other way around. Carbon lowers iron's melting point: pure iron melts at &b1538&r °C, cast iron with four percent carbon at &b1147&r, and that's exactly what makes the blast furnace possible. &6Tinkers&r puts steel above iron because it needs a ladder, not metallurgy. In a pack where the chemistry is real almost everywhere, it helps to know exactly where it stops being real.

Cobalt in &6Tinkers&r is designed as a Nether ore, but there's no ore in this world in any dimension. However, &6ChemLib&r has a cobalt ingot, and it sits in the same forge:ingots/cobalt tag the smeltery looks at. The metal will pass for the native one just as our steel did.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.89: Sixteen identical atoms make a pinch of dust, exactly as many as in an ingot. Dust into the furnace, ingot out: a workaround for when the direct recipe is busy with something else.
A hammer head is eight ingots
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.8b: A wall you can see through
A diamond comes at a price
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.8c: Every third level is a gift
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.8d: The &eCombiner&r works with formulas: it needs the composition to add up. The &eCompactor&r works with quantity: &b16&r identical atoms in, a piece of dust out, no reaction. Strictly speaking, that's no longer chemistry but physics. But this is exactly where the whole pack's scale closes the loop: &b16&r atoms make an ingot, and the ingot smelts back into the vanilla one in a furnace.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.8e: Water in, items out, and no buckets: the liquid arrives by pipe. Only what comes out isn't a gas but a molecule: &b500&r mB make eight chemlib:water. Splitting it into hydrogen and oxygen is the Dissolver's job, as a separate step. In real life that's electrolysis: current through water, hydrogen at the cathode, oxygen at the anode, exactly two to one.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.91: Experience comes from a source, and every tool has its own. Pickaxe, Sledge Hammer, Excavator: per block broken. Sword, Dagger, Cleaver: per damage dealt. Armor: per damage taken. Bow and Crossbow: per hit on a target.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.93: One &eCombiner&r means a queue. There are plenty of recipes ahead, the machine holds one active recipe at a time, and you'll be sick of switching it by hand by the third compound.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.97: No steel needed, no lava needed, made from the same stuff as the whole smeltery. You should have built it yesterday.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.98: Took the spectrum of White Antimatter
The slots work simultaneously, each with its own item. That's why the smeltery isn't one and a half times faster than the melter, it's as many times faster as you built it big.

Steel is the first material this world never had. And it's also the first material your fire can't take: you've made something more refractory than anything at your disposal. Lava isn't there to make the multiblock look pretty. Lava is there for the thousand degrees.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.99: Hepatizon: copper, cobalt and quartz, alloyed at &b1400&r. Lava gives a thousand. Nothing gives fourteen hundred except Blazing Blood, and blazes mean the Nether again. Which also explains why the mod has a fuel hotter than lava in the first place.

There isn't a single mob in this world. So everything that levels through combat stays at zero forever: the sword stays fresh and the armor new, however long you wear it. The only things that grow are the ones you pound the plain with.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.9a: Now try that on in our world. There isn't a single ore, all the rock is the same, and there's nothing in it to smelt. Luck doesn't double what never drops, and Autosmelt smelts thin air. The only thing worth anything here is what saves your time on the endless plain, and that isn't what the guides recommend.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.9d: One problem. There's no cobalt in the rock. The twenty-five elements that &eWhite Antimatter&r gives up end at platinum, and there's not a trace of number twenty-seven among them. So cobalt isn't mined here but synthesized, and that's chapter six.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.9e: It's far from just water. Ammonia, methane, ethane, ethanol, carbon dioxide, hydrogen sulfide, helium along with neon, argon, krypton, xenon and radon, and mercury, the only metal on the list that flows on its own. And three acids: hydrochloric, nitric and sulfuric.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.9f: The compound went into the Liquifier and came back out of the Atomizer
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.a0: One more reason to put materials into the pickaxe and the hammer rather than into weapons. There's nobody here to poke them at anyway.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.a2: A crafting table works too: &b8&r iron ingots in a ring, carbon in the center. That's &b128&r iron atoms instead of &b15&r. The recipe exists in case the &eCombiner&r is busy with something else, and for no other reason.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.a3: For two chapters you've been taking the world apart. Iron, silicon, carbon, oxygen: all of it was already lying under your feet, you just had to pull it out.

Don't look in JEI for the Tool Forge from older &6Tinkers&r versions: it can't be built in this version, and everything it did has moved to the anvil. If you miss the name, there's a recipe with a Tinker Station in the middle: it gives the very same anvil, just labeled “Tool Forge”.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.a4: There's one thing it can't do: hold liquid. A regular brick doesn't either, so you lose nothing, but glass can't take a fuel tank's place; that spot needs an actual tank.
A handle can go negative too
It's counted by interior blocks, the air inside the box, not the bricks outside. Each interior block adds &b1080&r mB to the tank and one item slot. Twelve ingots per block, if you measure in metal.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.a5: The press doesn't have a million years
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.a9: From here the cycle is complete: elements → ingot → molten metal → casting. The world didn't give you a single step of it.
There is no water in the world: no lakes, no rain, no ice. Every drop of water there will ever be here is put together by hand from two gases.
Set a drain and a chute into the smeltery wall
Expand the smeltery and see what changed in its window

Work out the carbon share by mass: it comes to &b1.4&r%%. Real carbon steel falls within &b0&r.&b02&r-&b2.1&r%%, and &b1.4&r is its upper half, the kind used for cutting tools and leaf springs. Nobody fudged this: the recipe was written to the “&b16&r atoms make an ingot” scale and landed in real metallurgy on its own.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.aa: Count the whole tool. A pickaxe is two plus one plus one: four ingots. A Sledge Hammer: eight for the head, three for the Tough Handle and four each for two Large Plates, nineteen in total. A steel hammer will cost almost three hundred iron atoms, and that's before any modifiers.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.ac: Everything interesting in &6Tinkers&r starts with molten metal. Without a melter the mod is just a set of wooden shovels.

There's no other source of lava in this pack at all. &6Thermal&r has a similar crucible, but Thermal Expansion didn't make it into the pack, so you won't find it in JEI. The smeltery, obsidian and this machine: there is no other road to steel.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.ad: The &eSpectrometer&r answers the question people ask most often in this pack: “what is this even made of?”
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.ae: The Part Builder cuts parts from solid materials: wood, stone, bone, flint, copper, glowstone. It won't take iron or steel, and that isn't balancing: you can't whittle a chunk of iron with a knife.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.b0: Build a Seared Melter and put it on the heater

Something else popping out means you need the fix from another chapter. Chapter &b2&r: the &eAtomizer&r, the &eLiquifier&r and the Industrial tiers of &6Alchemistry&r machines. Chapter &b3&r: the ME Controller, the Molecular Assembler and the Pattern Provider. Chapter &b4&r: the Cascade tiers of &6Alchemistry&r machines and everything for the fission reactor. Chapter &b5&r: the fusion controller and core, the &eQuantum Compressor&r. Chapter &b6&r: the Ultimate tables from &6Extended Crafting&r. Chapter &b7&r: the Antimatter Shard and &eAntimatter&r itself.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.b1: Find out where cobalt comes from in this world
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.b2: Stone head: &b130&r durability, speed &b4&r, damage &b1&r. Flint: &b85&r durability, speed &b3.5&r, damage &b1&r.&b25&r. On paper flint loses at everything except hitting, and the choice looks obvious.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.b3: Three other mods have steel, and none of them will help right now. &6Mekanism&r requires a Metallurgic Infuser, which needs osmium: sixteen atoms at a quarter-percent yield means six thousand blocks of rock dissolved before you build your first machine. &6NuclearCraft&r has the ingot in the game but no road to it at all: no recipe in the mod makes the steel dust its path starts with. TConstruct wants an entire smeltery.

So why have it? Because a material brings its trait to the tool, and the binding is the cheapest way to bring that trait in: one ingot versus two for a head. Flint gives Jagged, copper gives Dwarven, steel gives Ductile.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.b5: Understand why you need a smeltery when you already have a melter
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.b6: &6Tinkers&r Grout is almost real chamotte. The sand and gravel in it aren't filler: pure clay shrinks and cracks when fired, but cut with sand it holds. Kiln bricks have been made this way for several thousand years.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.b8: The faucet hangs on the drain, not on a brick. Pipes and hoppers connect to the chute. From this point on, the smeltery stops being a place you run to by hand with a full inventory.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.b9: The rule is simple: one machine, one recipe. The recipe lock is unreliable here: a pipe tops up a free slot and the lock drops; rejoin the server and it drops too. A do-everything station doesn't survive in this pack. Build a row of machines, each for its own job.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.bb: Got it: you pay for the walls, not the metal
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.bc: Silicon dust is no small thing. Half of chapter four rests on it: silicon goes into quartz, quartz into processors.

Classic &6Tinkers&r wants lava: the smeltery runs only on liquid fuel, and there's no lava in this world and nowhere to get it yet. The Seared Heater doesn't ask for lava at all: it heats a single melter sitting right on top of it. The multiblock won't run this way, but you can already pour metal.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.bd: Water went full circle: Combiner → Liquifier → Atomizer
Solid fuel gives &b800&r °C. Copper melts at &b500&r, gold at &b700&r, iron at exactly &b800&r: just barely, but it takes it.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.be: Composite casting doesn't work like the regular kind. You put a finished stone part on the casting table and pour &b125&r mB of molten clay over it. The part doesn't melt down: it becomes a seared stone part. One clay ball gives &b250&r mB, so that's enough for two.
“Gilded” is the only modifier that doesn't spend slots but swaps them: you give up your only ability and get two upgrades. For a pickaxe, which has one ability, that's a deal with no refunds.
Read it, not going to look
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.bf: Liquefy any compound other than water and collect it back

There's also the Seared Duct: the same drain, but with a filter. It only lets out the liquid that's in the bucket or Copper Can placed inside it. On a smeltery cooking three alloys at once, you can't sort them into separate tanks without it.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.c0: There's a third way too: three gravel on a crafting table. Your gravel costs one silica apiece, so it comes out to the same three. This recipe isn't in vanilla; &6Tinkers&r adds it.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.c4: &eCombiner&r: &b15&r iron and &b1&r carbon. A normal ingot has &b16&r iron atoms; here one of them gives up its place to carbon, and that single swap changes the metal's whole character.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.c5: A diamond at the station adds durability and raises the tier, and takes one of the three upgrade slots. An emerald does almost the same, except the bonus is calculated from base durability and pushes conditional traits like Jagged harder.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.c6: Hence the order of work. First build the tool from what you'll be using for a long time, and only then start leveling it. Do your experimenting on a separate pickaxe you won't miss.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.c8: Build a Seared Ingot Tank and a Seared Fuel Gauge
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.c9: Build a Tinker's Anvil. Optional branch
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.ca: For two chapters the &eDissolver&r and the &eCombiner&r came from the starter chest, because otherwise the game couldn't begin: the Dissolver is made of iron, and iron comes from dissolving. That was the only exception in the whole game.

Copper melts at &b500&r °C, and coal with its eight hundred has plenty to spare. So the entire smeltery, down to the last block, is built on coal, without a single drop of lava. That's exactly why the Copper Age came before the Iron Age: copper melts in a campfire.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.cc: Here's the main rule of modifiers, and it's the opposite of what you'd expect: a modifier doesn't add a slot, it spends one. The diamond takes one of three, leaving two for everything else.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.cd: Alloy four ingots each of bronze and invar

“Reinforced”, on the other hand, the one that stops a tool from wearing out, is made from an Emerald Reinforcement: 25 mB of molten emerald on obsidian glass. There's no emerald in the rock. So in this chapter Reinforced comes exactly one way: the tool you're leveling earns it. More on that below.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.cf: The &eCombiner&r assembles chemlib:water from two hydrogens and an oxygen. The Liquifier turns eight of those molecules into &b500&r mB of water, and the &eAtomizer&r turns it back into the same eight. The rate is fair both ways, so the loop closes at exactly zero in matter and at a loss in energy. There will be no perpetual motion machine.
A gold cast is made the opposite way from a sand one. You put a finished ingot on the casting table and pour &b90&r mB of gold over it: the ingot goes inside, the cast remains.
A handle doesn't add, it multiplies. Wood does nothing, steel gives five percent each to durability and speed, osmium plus twenty to durability and minus ten to speed.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.d0: So planks start with a sapling, and the sapling starts with the &eCombiner&r: oak, birch, spruce, acacia and dark oak are all in there. Dirt can be made too, and water comes from hydrogen and oxygen. Trees here are grown from atoms, and if you haven't done it yet, start now: you'll need wood more than once.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.d1: Fuel is spent not on how much you melt but on how big a box you heat. Consumption is one, plus one more for every fifteen blocks of walls and floor.
Got it: an ability trades for two upgrades
Iron, a piston, redstone, a cauldron and two stone pressure plates.

&cThere is no steel under your feet. There is none anywhere&r: steel only happens when someone measures out carbon for iron precisely. &aIt is the first thing in this world that will exist only because you decided it should.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.d2: Build a fuel tank, fire up the smeltery and melt steel
Alloy and cast 4 Rose Gold Ingots
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.d3: Clay melts at &b450&r, and a coal-fired melter handles it with plenty to spare: no smeltery or lava needed. The “Searing” trait: it chews faster through anything that can melt itself. We have no ores, but there's a lot of metal ahead.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.d4: Graphite and diamond are the same carbon; the only difference is how the atoms are stacked. In real life the second is made from the first with a press: one and a half million atmospheres and fifteen hundred degrees. The &eCompactor&r does exactly that, just without a pressure gauge.
A head made of it is worthless: &b175&r durability and gold tier. But speed &b9&r, faster than anything else in this chapter. And as a handle it takes away a third of the durability.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.d5: Steel melts at &b950&r. That's a separate conversation, further down the branch.

A pickaxe has three upgrade slots and one ability slot. The Sledge Hammer and the Excavator have two and one. The Dagger has three and one, the Longbow two and one. The bigger the tool, the less fits into it: that's how the mod balances the hammer against the pickaxe.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.d9: The conclusion is unpleasant but honest: a big smeltery only pays off when it's fully loaded. Running a &b5&r by &b5&r for three ingots is heating the street. And that's also why, in the end, you'll have to stop carrying lava in buckets and start cooking it continuously.

The point of &6Tinkers&r here isn't that the tools are tougher. It's that every part has its own material: a copper head digs fast and wears out, a steel one lasts twice as long. You don't pick a tool tier, you pick a composition: exactly the same logic as in the rest of the pack.

You can't make it on a crafting table. Set up a casting basin, put a Seared Bricks block in it and pour &b360&r mB of molten copper on top: four copper ingots' worth in the melter. The brick block gets used up.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.de: Build a tool whose binding was picked for its trait
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.e1: These modifiers don't take up slots. It's the only way around “three and one”, and also the only way to get Reinforced while there's no emerald in the world. It also explains why “Haste” says “Science!” in its description: redstone dust speeds things up, and nobody promised to explain why.

This is where the point begins. The station pulls ingredients from chests placed right next to it, shows them as tabs on the side, and doesn't forget the recipe you laid out when you close the window. In a chapter where every item is made from four others, that saves more time than any machine.

Alloys only happen in the smeltery. It has one shared tank for everything: pour in copper and gold, the proportions match, and rose gold appears on its own. The proportion here isn't a wish but a condition: the excess stays unmixed and just gets in the way.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.e2: So it pays to leave stone unrepaired while you're digging, and flint while you're fighting. In a mod where a tool is repaired with one click at the station, this is the first thing that makes you stop and think.
Add a diamond to a tool
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.e3: Two more went the same way. “Netherite” asks for a smithing template from a bastion. “Expanded”, which widens the hammer's reach, asks for amethyst bronze and two ichor: you'll alloy the bronze in this very chapter, but ichor is a liquid from the Nether, and the recipe won't come together without it.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.e4: A &b3&r by &b3&r smeltery two layers tall is eighteen interior blocks: eighteen slots and almost twenty buckets of capacity. Add a third layer and it's twenty-seven. The limit is fourteen by fourteen inside, and up to sixty-four high.
So a binding is chosen not by the stat table but by the trait line. It's the only part in the mod with no numbers to compare, because there aren't any.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.e9: A vanilla pickaxe runs out. This one is repaired with the same material at the station and lasts the whole game, and you'll be digging a lot here: the multiblocks of chapters five and six are big, and the rock around you is endless.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.eb: Seared Glass is a full-fledged wall: it goes in place of a brick and the multiblock accepts it. And you can see what's going on inside, which is the only way to figure out where the ingots you threw in went and why nothing is melting.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.ed: Same procedure as with the ingot: a wooden part from the Part Builder goes on the casting table, a Blank Sand Cast on top, the impression is taken, the part stays intact. Then you pour into that cast the metal the Part Builder can't cut, and this is where steel finally comes in.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.ee: It's made from Gilded Blackstone, and blackstone only exists in the Nether. The Nether is still two chapters away, so make a note and don't go looking.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.ef: Copper has the “Dwarven” trait: the deeper you dig, the faster the tool works and the farther arrows fly. Climb up high and the bonus turns negative.
Two traits that grow with wear
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.f0: &7Every new spectrum is written to the journal. The journal survives death, unlike your stuff.&r

One sand gives &b4&r Blank Sand Casts. Put a blank on the casting table and any ingot on top. No pouring needed: the impression takes itself and the ingot stays intact. Casts of tool parts are taken exactly the same way.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.f1: In the center is steel itself, the required path, which also grants the steel stage. On the left is the second line of &6Alchemistry&r machines, and from it a long &6Tinkers&r branch runs down, hiding the nastiest question of the chapter. On the right are the Tinkers workstations; they need wood, and there's no wood in the world either, so start with saplings.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.f2: Build a copper tool and read its trait
Two Patterns and two planks; a Pattern is planks and sticks, six at a time. Except there's no wood in the world.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.f3: Iron, pistons, redstone and two cauldrons. No steel needed.
Two hundred, then four hundred, then eight hundred
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.f4: The task doesn't check for an item, it checks for the #forge:ingots/steel tag. That's the whole quest.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.f5: Manyullyn: three parts cobalt to one part molten ancient debris. Netherite scrap melts into the same molten debris, and scrap is made in the &eCombiner&r from carbon and nobelium: there's no ancient debris ore in this world. The head: &b1250&r durability, &b3.5&r damage, netherite tier, the best metal &6Tinkers&r has to offer, and it's three chapters away.
That doesn't make it work just yet. The multiblock needs a tank of liquid fuel under its floor, and solid fuel means nothing to it. The next quest is about exactly that.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.f7: The gain is noisy too: there's a fifty-percent spread, so the same block can drip anywhere from nothing to double the usual amount. Over the long run it changes nothing, but in the first ten minutes it's confusing.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.f8: Iron in the corners, pistons top and bottom, magma blocks on the sides, a Steel Ingot in the center. The Magma Block doesn't come from the world either: it's &b4&r Magma Cream, and the cream is a slimeball and blaze powder, both made in the &eCombiner&r.
Melts at &b950&r. Exactly like steel: same threshold, same lava, same conversation.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.f9: A tool gathers experience on its own as it works. The first level costs two hundred points, and each one after that costs twice the previous: four hundred, eight hundred, sixteen hundred. The fifth will run you over three thousand; better not to count the tenth.
chemlib:carbon is the element, chemlib:graphite is the compound. The first one goes into steel.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.fa: Three Patterns and four planks. The Part Builder makes the parts, the station assembles the tool from them and applies modifiers: neither works without the other.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.fb: Without sand, gravel and clay there's no &6Tinkers&r Grout, and without Grout there's no smeltery and no casting. The whole left branch hangs on this.
The first material the world doesn't have
&b240&r atoms make &b16&r Steel Ingots. The &eDissolver&r will be spinning for a long while; automate it and work on the side branches in the meantime, they don't need steel.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.03_tools.fe: A swap doesn't touch modifiers at all, only experience. So trying out materials on a leveled tool is safe right up until you start missing the levels.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.04_industry: The type tabs are switched at the top of the pipe's window. Half of all “why isn't it pumping” questions are an unselected tab, and half of the rest are a forgotten upgrade.
An ME Pattern Provider right on the Combiner: the world starts taking itself apart

The third way to pull, and the most brazen. The node goes right against the machine, and neighboring nodes find each other on their own. To reach far, use a connector, and link them with the wrench, connector to connector.
Afterwards it's copied like the others: the press itself on top, an iron block in the middle. You won't have to gather a quarter million items a second time.

The Inscriber works in two passes. First the circuit: press on top, material in the middle (silicon for Printed Silicon, gold for Logic, certus for Calculation, diamond for Engineering). Then the circuit, Printed Silicon and redstone together.
Split one stream between two receivers with different priorities.
Chemistry can't tell isotopes apart. But that's a problem for Chapter 5.
The key word is silently. Only put it where you know for sure things will overflow, and never in a cell holding something you have exactly one of.

The &6AE2&r &6Alchemistry&r addon turns the Combiner into a crafting machine as AE2 understands it. The provider pushes not items into it, but the recipe itself: the machine takes its target from the incoming pattern, grinds through it and hands the result back to the provider, bypassing the output slots.
Faster, and from both sides
That's the whole point of subnetworks. The big network feeds power to a small utility one, and that one lives its own life, with its own controller or with none at all.
There's no output bonus, for the same reason as with the &eCombiner&r: sixteen atoms make one dust, and “sometimes two” is no longer technique.

The pattern for &eWhite Antimatter&r: &b16&r iron, &b8&r silicon, &b8&r carbon for four blocks. All of it is already in storage, because the Dissolver has been running without you since the middle of the chapter. Press “order” and just watch the network work out the tree.
Normally uraninite is mined. You're putting it together from atoms, and it's the first nuclear fuel you've ever made yourself.

A block of redstone, Fluix Dust and Sky Stone Dust have to be thrown into water on the ground. Not into a furnace, not into a machine, not into the Combiner: just into water, and it will fuse on its own.

A classic everyone gets to eventually, usually late. An interface from the main network faces into the subnet, a storage bus in the subnet is placed on it, and the subnet sees all of your storage without taking up a single channel outside.
Did the math. AE2 cells won't cover this
Every inserting connector has a priority. The higher the number, the sooner it gets served. High for the &eCombiner&r, low for the chest, and storage takes exactly what the machine didn't eat.

Just don't pull recipes into it with a shift-click on the JEI transfer button. On this version that transfer duplicates items, gets caught the very first time, and can't be disabled from scripts. On the server, it ends with a conversation with the admins. Lay it out by hand, or leave it all to the provider; it doesn't have that button.

Useful once the workshop has grown and half of it is needed once a week. A disconnected branch takes no channels and eats no energy, and the controller's appetite is steady and round-the-clock, unlike that of &6Alchemistry&r machines.
No pipes, no cables
Quantum ring
One controller, one network

For autocrafting this is even more convenient than before: you need an ordinary &6AE2&r pattern for a single batch, and the machine simply finishes it sixteen times faster. No need to inflate the pattern, and nowhere to: the input slot holds no more than a stack anyway.

That's how rows of machines get fed: one subnet per workshop, eight channels inside it, one interface sticking out. And the question “why did I run out of channels again” solves itself along the way.

It takes longer to set up than Pipez, but all the logic runs in one block instead of in every pipe separately. Twenty Dissolvers on one controller cost the server about as much as one.
The recipe is shapeless and remarkably cheeky: a water bucket, two cacti, bone meal, silicon, a slimeball and glowstone dust, all in one pile. Everything here is synthetic, right down to the cactus.
&b48&r of them on a single Inscriber will take a while. Three in parallel solve the problem. Later the network will learn to make them itself, but the network is built from them too.

The terminal runs on power and drains. Keep a charger next to the access point, or it'll die exactly when you're three hundred blocks of white plain away from storage.

Same tiers: four and sixteen times faster, price by the number of machines replaced. It asks for little energy: fifty FE per tick at base, so two hundred and eight hundred on the tiers. Next to the Cascade &eCombiner&r's thirty-two hundred, that's nothing, and here you pay not in power but in machine casings.
Build a Charger and make an Inscriber Energy Press in it.
Place them precisely, at the bottleneck. Otherwise one day you'll find a quarter of your reactor going to speed up a conveyor that was keeping up fine without it.

The price is fair: four Industrial ones, which is sixteen regular Dissolvers. There's no saving on materials, and none was intended: the whole benefit is that your base has one block instead of sixteen.

The exact opposite of an &6AE2&r cell. There it's sixty-three types and a byte limit; here it's one type and no limit at all. Place it by a conveyor, and it takes in everything that rolls past.
Feed the condenser 256,000 items and get a Singularity.
The 256M cell
There is a fifth press after all
By default a card stirs once every twenty ticks. The overclocker shortens the pause and increases the batch, but the node starts eating FE, and the more cards are overclocked, the more it eats.
Without it there's no autocrafting at all. The provider won't start, because there's nobody to unfold the order “give me a steel block” into a tree of a hundred operations.
&eCombiner&r: &b4&r uranium and &b8&r oxygen. Uranium comes out of rock rarely, so stockpile it in advance or set up a second &eDissolver&r.
The access point broadcasts the network through the air, and the terminal picks it up. The radius is small; boosters go into the access point and stretch it, and each one costs more than the last.
Hands off

The &6MEGA&r provider holds far more patterns than the regular one, and that's exactly what a Combiner with a hundred recipes needs. But its tooltip honestly warns you: it only understands Processing.
Drag the recipe into the terminal straight from JEI with the transfer button. Quantities are checked down to the single item, and if they don't match, the order simply won't go. Silently.
&aThis quest unlocks the chapters “Core”, “Industrial Chemistry”, “Ad Astra”, “The Otherside”, “Malum”, “RFTools” and “Hostile Networks”.&r

&7The set used to be given as a reward, and the description carried a warning: “don't lose it, there'll be no way to replace it.” Now losing it is no big deal: just make it again.&r

&6Alchemistry&r machines happen to have their input and output on different faces. That's the difference between one connector and two connectors with an extra bit of cable wrapped around the Dissolver.
Storage for power
Machine first, surplus to the chest
Remember this feeling. In Chapter 7 you'll find out that the living lacks exactly one element, and that element isn't in the table.
On the standard &6AE2&r path you throw seeds into water and wait. There's no water here, so the crystals aren't grown but assembled. This isn't bypassing progression; this is the progression.
Get 8 Sky Steel Ingots. You'll need lava, and there's none here.
You'll need latex either way: without it you can't build a single addon or any machine frame above the starter one.
Two controllers on one network bring the whole thing down: it goes into conflict and shuts off. Just one, even if you really want a second for reliability.
The addon covered chemistry; the assembler covers the crafting table. Together they close the whole chain: elements, compounds, parts, blocks.
And look at the interface before you place it. The reactor needs cooling, and all the water in this world is synthetic: the very same water from the chapter about the bucket.
Set priorities on the drive and the storage bus.

One order takes up a whole CPU: while it's working out the plastic, a second craft waits. One is enough for this chapter, but give it plenty of memory.
&6Alchemistry&r machines don't hand anything over to anyone. &6What pulls, works; what waits to be handed something, doesn't.&r
Set it up once
Chemical cells work like item cells: the housing separately, the component separately, tiers from &b1k&r to &b256k&r. There are portable ones too, and a chemical P2P tunnel.
Rock gives it up generously, a &b12&r%% yield. All the electronics on the planet are made of this element, and yours will be too.

A regular filter says what may be carried. This tool says where exactly: poke the chest you want with it, and the rule stops applying to the whole main line.
Craft four Card Overclockers.

Hence automation without a single repeater. The reactor shuts down when the energy cell is full. The &eDissolver&r stops when there's too much rock in storage. And the wire is the very same cable that carries items.

Fluix has no formula: it's an &6AE2&r invention, and the Combiner recipe is put together by what makes sense. Redstone, on the other hand, is no invention: iron oxide with strontium, and it's red for exactly the same reason strontium colors fireworks.
Still sixty-three types. &6MEGA&r solves volume, not variety: for three hundred types you still need ten-odd cells, it's just that each of them is now bottomless.
There was a pattern here somewhere

Provider right against the Combiner, pattern inside, order from the terminal.

&eCombiner&r: kaolinite and graphite. The mod's usual recipe asks for clay and coal; here both come from elements, like everything in this world.
A press made of two presses

In a normal game the four Inscriber presses lie in a chest inside a meteorite. Here the world is a flat plane of four layers of antimatter on &ebedrock&r, structures are disabled entirely, and no meteorite will &cever&r fall.
The range is limited, and the wrench will honestly tell you when you've overshot. Don't stretch it across half the base right away: first two blocks side by side, then extend.

If something else is popping out, you need the fix from another chapter. Chapter &b2&r: the &eAtomizer&r, the &eLiquifier&r and the Industrial tiers of &6Alchemistry&r machines. Chapter &b3&r: the ME Controller, the Molecular Assembler and the Pattern Provider. Chapter &b4&r: the Cascade tiers of &6Alchemistry&r machines and everything for the fission reactor. Chapter &b5&r: the Fusion Chamber Controller and Fusion Core, the &eQuantum Compressor&r. Chapter &b6&r: the Ultimate tables from &6Extended Crafting&r. Storage in your pocket
From liquid to solid

A regular cable carries eight channels, a dense one thirty-two, and each face of the controller hands out thirty-two. A device occupies its channel along the whole path to the controller, not just right next to itself.
Its interface has an Auto-eject toggle, and the tooltip promises the output will go into an adjacent chest. &cThe toggle is there, and it doesn't work.&r &7Don't waste an evening on it.&r

That's the bare minimum to serve a Dissolver without a single pipe: a strip of conveyor, an extraction upgrade at the machine, an insertion upgrade at the chest. Cheaper than Pipez and much easier to see.
The smart cable differs in that it shows occupied channels as colored stripes. It costs exactly the same, and everyone ends up hunting for where exactly the channels ran out, and more than once.
Chest of rock → Dissolver → extraction → chest of elements.
A cell has two limits. Types: always sixty-three, whatever the label says. Bytes: exactly what the label says (1k, 4k, 16k, 64k, 256k).
The storage block holds an order's intermediate items. If there isn't enough, the network will say the order is too big and won't start at all.
Build a Fluid Extractor and a Latex Processing Unit.

Bone meal is the only thing the world doesn't give you directly. But a composter takes any greenery, and greenery grows from seeds you already know how to assemble from sucrose. The finished resin must go into a furnace: only the baked resin is in the ingot tag, and the raw one won't fit anywhere.
The terminal shows every provider on the network and everything in them in one list. You can move patterns between providers right from here, without taking the workshop apart.
Processing only
Click the checkmark and claim the reward, and the stage will be granted again. If you already have it, nothing changes: granting it twice is harmless.
A setup that works for the whole game: partitioned cells for elements at high priority, a general dump at low. Then iron won't spread in a thin layer across every cell in a row.
The Fuzzy Card makes a bus ignore tool durability and, if you ask, different variants of the same item. The Inverter Card flips the filter: instead of “only this” you get “everything except this”.
The monitor goes on a cable and shows the count of one chosen item right in the wall. Lock it with a wrench, or you'll knock it off with a stray click by day two.
On its own it pulls nothing: items have to fall onto it. The first quest's rule holds even here.

The Compression Card makes it even bolder: the cell starts counting nuggets, ingots and blocks of the same metal as one substance, and the output module breaks the chain back down when the network needs an ingot but only has a block.
Build a Pity Black Hole Unit.

This stage gates the Cascade tiers of &6Alchemistry&r machines and everything for the fission reactor. It's easy to tell this is your case: the quest is completed, the reward is claimed, but these items still pop out of your inventory and can't be picked up off the ground. That means the grant command didn't fire.
Collect 8 Industrial Foregoing Plastic.

Right next to it is a limit: “don't insert if the receiver already has more than N”. It's the cheapest way to keep one stack in a machine instead of a mountain of rock you'll later have to fish out by hand.
Craft a MEGA Item Cell Housing and a 1M MEGA Item Storage Cell.
Kitchen-table lithography
Craft a Fuzzy Card and an Inverter Card.

Lava doesn't exist in this world. No lakes, no buckets, no recipe, not a single block in all four layers under your feet. The only place it exists is beyond the portal to the Nether, and that's the next chapter.
Further along the chapter come the &6AE2&r controller, Inscribers and processor crafting. They draw power constantly, not just when you press a button.
There is no lava here

What trips everyone up: the addon only knows the &eCombiner&r and the &eCompactor&r, the rest still need pipes or buses; turn on blocking mode on the provider, or the network will shove a second order into a busy machine; the pattern must be a Processing Pattern, and exactly matching the recipe; don't combine a manual recipe lock and a provider on the same machine.
The Compactor too
A regular terminal shows your storage. The crafting one adds a three-by-three grid and pulls ingredients from storage by itself, no dragging needed.
Build an ME Controller and an Energy Acceptor.
Craft an ME Toggle Bus and an ME Inverted Toggle Bus.

Eight plastic is &b256&r PVC, and every PVC is itself assembled from carbon, hydrogen and chlorine. Set up a pattern for PVC, a pattern for plastic, and order eight in one request: the network will unfold the tree on its own.
Craft an Energy Cell and eight cables.
The machine first, the rest in the corner

A familiar scheme from the third quarter of the chapter: press plus Charged Redstone gives a printed circuit, and the circuit with Printed Silicon and ordinary redstone gives a processor. The Charged Redstone comes from that same Charger.
The others in the same family: the splitting upgrade divides the stream in a set ratio, the detection upgrade emits redstone when an item passes, the dropping upgrade drops everything down.
The third link of the same chain
The press does have a recipe, but it's self-referential: a press plus an iron block in the Inscriber gives a copy of &lthe same&r press. You can multiply them, but you can't get the first one.
The controller has exactly eight channels. A channel's type is assigned once and for good: items, fluid, energy or logic. You can't mix them in one.

The reactor needs not just fuel but cooling too. Check its interface to see what it asks for: if it's water, remember that this world has exactly as much water as you've synthesized yourself. You'll have to pour it in here and not be stingy.
Craft four Quartz Fiber.
Got it: pull, don't wait

&6Alchemistry&r machines eat in bursts: during an operation they draw power, between operations they don't. The &6AE2&r controller is the opposite: it draws steadily, and any dip in power takes the whole network down.
The controller eats energy and simply sits silent without it. Power comes from the &6Powah&r branch on the left.
Crafting table: iron, a block of redstone and logs in the corners. The logs are where anyone who skipped Chapter 1 will trip up: there isn't a single tree in this world, the biome doesn't grow them.
The chest is empty. Confirmed
The chapter's rule hasn't gone anywhere: a card in Extract mode pulls, a card in Insert mode puts. The machine still doesn't make the first move.
Charged quartz, an iron ingot and a Sky Stone block have to be thrown into lava. Not into a furnace, not into a machine: into lava.
The top of the &6MEGA&r storage ladder and a line on the &eCertificate&r transcript.
It's made from four 64M components, so the whole ladder has to be climbed for real, from bottom to top.

Craft an XNet Controller, Network Cable and Connectors.
Make 16 Dielectric Paste.
Processing, not Crafting
So the terminal doesn't flicker

Each face of the node is a separate slot. A card placed in the face looking at the Dissolver works with the Dissolver. The same card in a different face works with a different block, and that catches everyone out.
A chest right against the Dissolver's output face, Auto-eject on, rock inside. You come back: the machine is sitting there with full output slots, and the chest is empty.
A network inside a network
You can't get here too early: the fix only unlocks after the quest that grants the stage in the first place.
Combining has to keep the same pace

The network doesn't put things in the nearest storage or the emptiest one, but in the one with the highest priority that the item fits into at all. The number is set on the drive and on each storage bus separately.
Craft an Improved and an Advanced Pipe Upgrade.
Set up a filter so only what you need goes down the pipe.
A service quest. It exists for one case only: the “industry” stage was supposed to arrive as a reward, but didn't.
Two things you won't figure out on your own. Click the belt with glowstone dust and it runs faster. Click it with plastic and items on it stop getting picked up, so you can walk past in peace.
Speeding up dissolving and leaving combining as it was just moves the jam. Atoms will pile up faster than the &eCombiner&r can turn them into anything useful.
Hence the rule you'll be applying until the end of the game: many small cells for elements, one big one for iron.

So for elements, use many small cells, not one big one. By Chapter 7 you'll have &b118&r elements and around a hundred and fifty compounds; there's no sorting that into chests, neither physically nor in terms of search time.
Craft an Item Pipe, a Basic Pipe Upgrade and a Pipe Wrench.

Matter here lives in two forms. As a liquid it's pumped through pipes and comes from &6Mekanism&r chemistry; as a solid it's handled by the &eDissolver&r and the &eCombiner&r. The &eAtomizer&r turns the first into the second, the Liquifier does the reverse.
It doesn't stop at channels. Items, fluids, FE, redstone and even light each get their own tunnel, and all of them ride the same cable as the network itself.

The accessor pulls energy out of the network: run an ordinary cable to it, and from there it's just an FE source. The Induction Card does the reverse: an &6AE2&r device with one starts accepting and giving off energy on its own.
Craft a Filter Destination Tool and bind a rule to a single receiver.
The same Charger makes charged quartz, and charged quartz makes fluix. If you still don't have one set up, now's the time: from here on you'll need it constantly.
They're worth exactly as much as the number of parallel machines you have. Sixteen co-processors for a single Combiner won't do anything except punch a hole in your silicon stock.
Build the Quantum Link Chamber

It has to be fed accordingly: it eats rock four times as fast, and the supply has to keep up. But you don't need to keep four times the stock in its slot: the tier shortens the cycle, it doesn't inflate the batch.
The acceptor is where &6Powah&r power enters the network; the controller is its heart.
Craft a Redstone Proxy and set up a logic channel.

They all need latex, so the extractor goes in before the chamber. And keep in mind ahead of time: the next machine frame asks for nether bricks, and there's nowhere to get them in this world. The &6Industrial Foregoing&r machine branch hits the portal wall exactly the way sky steel does.
That's how one pipe serves five machines without mixing up who gets what. Without it, one day you'll run five separate pipes and you'll be hunting for the one the sulfur got stuck in.
Craft four Advanced Connectors.
Get 4 Redstone Crystals.
The blocks go right against each other, in any shape. A storage block is mandatory: the crafting plan is kept in it, while the Crafting Unit is just a casing.
Two hundred and fifty-six thousand
Build a Cell Workbench and partition one cell.
By hand this takes a terminal and an hour and a half of your life. The port does the same while you go about your business, and it doesn't drop items on the floor when you miss a slot.

In our pack the recipe has been changed: the center of the ring, which the mod left empty, is now taken by the &6Create&r PRECISION MECHANISM. The one item in the pack you can't put together by hand sits in the middle of the one thing that links worlds.

But the &eCombiner&r gets no output bonus, and that's not an oversight. The &eDissolver&r pulls atoms out of endless rock, and how many it gets is a matter of tuning. The Combiner, though, puts sixteen iron atoms into one ingot. “Sometimes two ingots from the same sixteen atoms” isn't technique anymore, it's a violation of the conservation law the whole pack stands on.
One instead of four

Every &6Powah&r crystal goes through it, and every upper tier of the mod goes through the crystals. Niotic is assembled from graphite, Spirited from beryl with chromium and vanadium: both are already bridged, so you don't need to grow them, only to energize them.
Eight and not one more
The orb isn't a block, it's a structure: the orb itself and the rods around it that shine into it. The higher the rods' tier and the more of them there are, the faster the recipe goes.
One rule the whole chapter rests on.

On its left side you switch between two encoding modes. &6Alchemistry&r machines need Processing: inputs on the left, output on the right, no crafting grid. A Crafting pattern will go off to a Molecular Assembler and will never work in the Combiner, and it'll look like “the addon is broken”.
Craft an Item, a Fluid and an Energy P2P Tunnel.
&eCombiner&r: silica, manganese and redstone.
Load a stack of rock, walk away, come back. Chest full: chapter understood. Chest empty and the machine clogged: you've hooked up something that waits to be fed.
Make 16 Certus Quartz Crystals.
By now the network already works out orders, so the difference between them is the difference between “make one thing on the spot” and “walk over and get it”. You won't want to go back.

But don't put a Storage Bus on an &6Alchemistry&r machine. The network will take it for storage and start stuffing random things into its free slots, and that stuffing makes the machine lose its selected recipe. The Storage Bus goes on a chest.
Craft 16 Fluix ME Smart Cable.
Fiber is the only thing that connects two &6AE2&r networks without making them one. Only energy passes through it: channels, items and orders don't.

Sixty-three types per cell. There are a hundred and eighteen elements, nearly a hundred and seventy-five &6ChemLib&r compounds, plus everything the mods add. Three hundred types is five full cells just for raw materials, and not a single byte left for stock.
Craft four ME P2P Tunnels and a Memory Card.

It also lifts the “one machine, one recipe” limit. Before, every recipe needed its own Combiner with a locked target, and the lock kept resetting on its own too. Now the pattern sets the target, fresh every time, and there's nothing left to reset.
Check the cable separately. The bottleneck in a workshop is almost always the cable, not the storage: a basic cable will happily choke a hardened cell, and it looks like “the reactor is weak”.

In our pack the recipe also includes an &eUltimate Component&r from &6Extended Crafting&r, the very mod whose table assembles the &eUltimate Singularity&r and the &eCertificate&r. Two kinds of storage meet in a single slot.
A button in the corner partitions the cell by what's already in it. Sort the elements by hand once, and from then on the order keeps itself.
The subnet sees storage through the interface
&6Draconic Evolution&r needs the Engineering Processor too: it sits at the center of every Draconium Core in place of the diamond.
Make an Inscriber Accumulation Press.
One type. Exactly one, partitioned with the same Cell Workbench. But it doesn't even show the amount as a number: the tooltip just says “a lot”, and that's an honest answer.

Cells, cables and generators have a capacitor inside, and it's the capacitor that sets both capacity and throughput. From the outside the tiers are nearly indistinguishable; the difference only shows in the tooltip numbers.

While only a bucket or two passes through it, speed doesn't matter. It starts to matter when there's a factory on the other side and all of its output has to be turned into items: five hundred millibuckets per cycle, and a cycle two and a half seconds long.
Make 16 AE2 Silicon.
Speeding up the first two and leaving the third just moves the jam one step further. Atoms will pile up in front of the Compactor exactly the way they piled up in front of the &eCombiner&r.
The cell goes into the same ME Drive as your items. From this moment on, the network stores FE exactly the way it stores iron: in bytes, with tiers from 1k to 256k.
The Combiner crafted an order from the network
For three chapters you picked the recipe in the machine. Now the order picks it, and the machine is just a tool.
Fluix makes cables, and cables hold the whole network together.
Put a provider on the Compactor too.
Energy by mail
If one provider serves both, Blocking Mode will start holding up the crafting-table recipes: the provider will wait for the Combiner to free up. Noticed a queue? Split it across two.
I know you'll check it anyway. Better now, in five minutes, than a week from now, when something stalls and you remember this button.
So without a working &6Create&r line, you can't build the ring. The mechanism is covered in Chapter 16.
By the end of the chapter the Dissolver runs without you, and storage fills faster than it's used up. The card goes into a drive or a bus and silently destroys whatever no longer fits.

A &6Powah&r Energy Cell holds a reserve and gives it to a cable. This one holds a reserve and gives it to the network, and the network hands it out to everything connected. The difference is that you have one drive, and it's already in place.

There's only one water in this world: the water you synthesized and poured out of a bucket. Make a separate puddle, fence it off and don't fill it in: you'll need it more than once, and not only for this branch.

Each next reactor puts out more and eats accordingly. Count consumption, not output: fuel here isn't dug up but assembled from atoms, and on the upper tiers uraninite goes faster than you can make it.

The Binding Card comes in two kinds, and not for decoration: the regular one works within a single world, and only the dimensional one works across a dimension border. In Chapter 5 you'll get a portal, and there's no running a cable from the generators beyond it to here.
