Reactors multiply only through the Nether. &aThis chapter is about how to stop fearing this place and start living in it.&r
A &eFusion Core&r is six tungsten ingots and three ancient debris. A chamber needs three cores. Nine debris per chamber.
No deal with this one
Shroomlight gives the same &b16&r phosphorus, plus chitin, plus phosphoric acid. And unlike glowstone, it can be grown.
Nether Wart Block: &b36&r germanium and &b36&r selenium. Warped Wart Block: &b4&r neodymium and &b4&r mercury. Not a single element in common except chitin.
Got it: reactors multiply only through the Nether

But after the first handful it pays for itself forever: plant it on soul sand, it grows without light or water and gives two to four per plant. It has a &eCombiner&r recipe too (&b4&r selenium, &b4&r germanium and chitin), but the garden bed is cheaper.
Go in wearing gold. Piglins shoot crossbows, there are lots of them, and they call each other for help.
Back the same way. Bring spare pearls: you print them at home, not here.
Got it: Nether recipes are symmetrical
Crystals first
One quartz is &b16&r barium. Five hundred and twelve is thirty-two quartz, half a stack.

Piglins still love gold: they'll take an ingot and stare at it. But there's no bartering in season two. They have nothing to give back, and the Easy Piglins glass box has been removed from the recipes.
The loop closes through fusion. Mendelevium is &b101&r, and &b101&r is &b50&r plus &b51&r, tin and antimony. You have mountains of tin after diorite, and antimony can be made from anything.
Collect 16 bottles of Dragon's Breath
Two gases from one bottle, and both of them are the real thing.
Visit the Crimson Forest
After that, it's fusion only: any element from any other. But first you need to have at least one.
There's more blackstone here and it mines faster than basalt, so haul blackstone.
Turns out you can take it with you
It gives more experience than everything else in this pack put together.

In the entire Dissolver, barium comes only from quartz and things made from quartz. In season two there's no quartz ore and no bartering: quartz is assembled from silica and barium. So all the barium you will ever have comes from the Fusion Chamber.
By the way, the cobblestone doesn't have to be the stone kind: the stand also takes blackstone, and bastions have mountains of it.

Thorium is fuel. &6NuclearCraft&r can run on it, and in real life people tried building reactors on it too: there's three times more of it on the planet than uranium, and it doesn't produce weapons-grade plutonium. It never took off, for reasons that have nothing to do with chemistry.
Throw a pearl into the hole
That's how these two dimensions are chained together. Every dragon respawn costs four ghasts, and every new batch of oganesson costs one respawn. Polonium buys oganesson.
Crying obsidian has no way back: there's no recipe to assemble it. Regular obsidian goes together and comes apart evenly, but this one only goes one way.
You can still offend them, and there are exactly two ways to do it: open a chest in front of them or break a gold block. Then no armor will save you: the whole bastion comes running.

And most importantly: a rod only drops from a blaze that a player finished off. That's literally what the loot table says. Lava, crushers, mob grinders: none of them will give you a single rod. They'll only give you experience, and not even that.
And haul it home. Blazes are blaze rods, rods are Fission Cores, and a Fission Core will never come together without them. A spawner at your base means you build new chambers without leaving home.
Iridium drops from nowhere else in this world. Not from the white rock, not from stone, not from the Nether apart from this block, not from the End. One item in the whole game, and this is it.
Hit the bottom one

Xenon is an anesthetic gas. It doesn't react with anything at all and changes nothing in the body; exactly how it switches consciousness off still hasn't been fully explained. It's also what pushes ion engines: almost every deep-space probe of the last twenty years flies on xenon.
Puts you to sleep and seeps through
Kill 32 wither skeletons
In the entire Dissolver there are exactly two elements that have only one source each, and both are in the Nether.
Kill 8 ghasts and collect 4 tears
Magma cream is blaze powder and a slimeball. There are no slimes in this world, but the slimeball gets printed: two sucrose and two protein.

You'll be coming back here for a long time, and here's why. By now chemistry has caught up with the Nether on almost everything: quartz gets printed, obsidian gets printed, skulls get printed, the star gets printed. But a Fission Core takes three blaze rods and a Fusion Core takes three ancient debris, and neither the rod nor the debris has a reverse recipe. A chamber needs three cores. So every new chamber, fission or fusion, means nine trips down.
A garden bed instead of a pickaxe
There will be no milk
Collect 27 Ancient Debris: that's three Fusion Chambers
A chest that follows you around
Breaks with everything inside
On average a block yields one and a half gold plus a handful of oxides on top. Nine independent groups is the maximum in the whole mod; no other recipe has more.
Bring back 16 Crying Obsidian
The frame, though, is nowhere to be had.
Beds explode here
It hangs in an item frame at the ship's stern, guarded by a shulker, and that's the only place in the whole game you'll find it.
Take the elytra from the ship
Milk cures Wither, but there's no milk in this world: there are no cows. So it's healing potions, armor, and never letting them get close.
Five climates

A huge blackstone ruin that comes in four types: bridge, hoglin stables, housing units and treasure room. Every one of them has chests, and that's the best loot in the Nether: the netherite upgrade template, enchanted books, diamonds, saddles.
Blue fog, howling, bones sticking out of the ground, and skeletons that shoot out of the fog at every sound.
Stockpile 64 each of xenon and radon
The magma block stands apart: two rolls on its own table, with an &b8&r%% chance of two lead. Lead drops from nowhere else in this pack, and Reactor Glass is lead plus silica.
Except for two lines in two recipes.

Polonium was discovered by Marie Skłodowska-Curie and named after Poland, which wasn't on the map at the time. It was the first element found by its radiation alone: nobody saw it or weighed it, they just noticed that the pitchblende was more radioactive than it had any right to be.
Eight boxes is nine stacks in one stack. One trip into the city, one trip back.
Get 3 Wither Skeleton Skulls
He gives half the experience the dragon does, and that's the best one-time experience in the Nether.

Quartz is printed. Obsidian is printed. Pearl, shell, skull, powder, tear, soul sand, wart, star: all printed. Germanium, barium, thulium, polonium, lutetium, lead, tungsten: all synthesized. Chemistry has caught up with the Nether on every point, and there's no reason to go there for resources anymore.
And these go one way
Nine groups in a row
Get to the End

Soul sand and soul soil dissolve the same way: one thulium and four silica, guaranteed. Thulium drops nowhere else in the whole world: not from the rock, not from stone, not from the End. Only from here.
Four blocks of soul sand in a T shape, three skulls on top, and the last thing you place is a skull.
Collect 36 blaze rods
Wear at least one piece of gold

The rest of the chain is already yours. Water is the recipe from the first chapter, the only water in the whole game. A bottle is three glass. Nether wart grows on soul sand and asks for neither light nor water. Water plus wart is an Awkward Potion, awkward plus magma cream is Fire Resistance.
The breath doesn't go back together: there's no recipe. What the dragon has exhaled can't be taken back.
Build a Beacon
A hundred and forty-four ingots in block form is a good stockpile. Load the chamber and go do something else.
The only two places in the whole game with real terrain underfoot, and only chemistry can get you there
The drink your body won't absorb
Twelve blocks that don't exist
Gateways open after the dragon and hang in the air as small black cubes in a ring around the central island.
Reach the Basalt Deltas and bring back 64 blackstone

The membrane can be printed: &b8&r cerium. But in the entire Dissolver, cerium comes from exactly one item: the membrane itself. A loop, and fusion breaks it: &b58&r is &b29&r plus &b29&r, copper plus copper, and you get copper from the white rock at four percent per block.
Fire Resistance is brewed like this: water, nether wart, magma cream. Magma cream is slime plus blaze powder. Blaze powder is a blaze rod. The brewing stand is a blaze rod too.
Smelt 16 blocks into Smooth Quartz
Make 64 Purpur Blocks
Visit the Nether Wastes
Haste at level four is the only thing that makes digging in this world bearable. You dig the white rock by the ton and you'll always be digging it: it's endless, and everything else comes from it.
And here it's simply exhaled. No reactor, no chain, no energy: the dragon breathes, you hold out a bottle. The only way to number &b118&r without a Fusion Chamber in the entire game.
This whole chapter is about packing eating your material. Here it's the other way around, and it's the only such case.

So the Ender Chest is made entirely from elements, without ever meeting a blaze or visiting the End. And it's the only logistics that works across the dimension border: put one down at home, take a second one with you and drop your loot in right where you dug it up.
All the iridium in the world
Kill 32 shulkers
Same forest, same fungus, same cap, only blue. And completely different chemistry.

The only vanilla storage that breaks with its contents inside and doesn't spill them on the floor. In the End that's not a convenience, it's the only way to bring anything back at all: the city stands on towers, below the towers is the void, and anything that falls out is gone forever.
In the Dissolver, one bottle gives &b8&r xenon, &b8&r radon and &b8&r oganesson.

And here's the funny part. There isn't a single mob on the white plain; every spawn list is empty. But phantoms come anyway: they don't come from the biome, they come from you not having slept in a while. In a world with nobody in it, at night there will still be someone above you.
Kill 64 endermen
For the first few seconds he's invulnerable, and then he explodes. Step back.
Bring back and dissolve 64 blocks of Nether Bricks

The Eye of Ender can be printed entirely. Pearl: &b16&r silicon, &b16&r mercury, &b16&r neodymium. Powder: &b8&r sulfur, &b8&r germanium, &b2&r graphite. You no longer need to visit a blaze or an enderman for these: the Combiner assembles both.
Pick up a blaze spawner with Silk Touch and take it away
And at the very bottom of the table there's a row with a weight of two out of three hundred and fifty-seven: thorium. Half a percent per block, roughly one in a hundred and seventy-eight.
Let's sum up.

The mod split red and blue across the whole biome. Crimson roots and weeping vines give mercury sulfide: cinnabar, the very red pigment used to paint everything from tombs to canvases. Warped roots and twisting vines give copper chloride, which burns green and so ends up in every other signal flare.
One rod is two powder. One powder is &b8&r germanium, &b8&r sulfur and &b2&r graphite.
Reach the Warped Forest and bring back 16 wart blocks
So the only place to get a second one is a second city. And so you'll have to repair it.
Something will fly in after all
Put it in the ceiling

Piglins don't check for a full set, only for the fact: wear at least one piece of gold and you're one of them, wear none and you're a stranger. Boots are cheaper than a helmet and don't get in the way.

Fission Core: six yttrium ingots and three blaze rods. &eFusion Core&r: six tungsten ingots and three ancient debris. Nothing assembles a rod. Nothing assembles debris. A chamber needs three cores, so every new chamber means nine trips down, always, to the end of the game.
Bring back 256 End Stone
The Dissolver spins regular blackstone like a roulette wheel: nine groups compete with each other, exactly one comes up, and you get one item.
One golden boot
It's not the shulker that kills you
Understand why there won't be an automatic blaze farm
Beds work here too, and they're still the fastest way. Also the fastest way to die.
First the crystals on the towers; the caged ones can be shot with an arrow through the bars. While even one is intact, the dragon heals faster than you can hit it.
Don't look them in the eye, stand under a two-block ceiling, hit them in the legs.
Take apart and reassemble any Nether item
Collect 64 Nether Wart
So in this chemistry netherite isn't an alloy, it's packaging. Handy packaging, too: a stack of scrap is a stack of scrap, but a stack of ingots is four stacks of scrap in one slot.
In season one, this line was why the Nether never ended. In season two chemistry caught up with it too: every new chamber costs nine debris, which is thirty-six scrap made from nobelium.
Twenty-seven is three Fusion Chambers. There's no ore in the Nether either, so you won't be digging, only assembling.
Two elements, two sources
The quartz block is a dead end

Calcium carbonate is chalk, limestone, eggshell and seashell, all the same substance. So the mod thinks the shulker is a mollusk, and if you think about it, that's the only sensible explanation for how it's built.

The plane you live on generates no structures at all, not a single one: no villages, no mineshafts, no stronghold with a portal. The twelve frame blocks don't exist anywhere in this world. Don't look for them, save yourself an evening: you have the eye, but there's no lock.
You've been here once
Glowstone gives &b16&r phosphorus per block and that's it: it doesn't grow, you have to find it on the ceiling and knock it down.
Fire resistance can be brewed after all
Grow 4 Wither Roses
Hitting it is pointless: it teleports a few blocks away. You take it with a piston: push it, it drops onto a torch, pick it up.

A netherite ingot is four scrap and four gold ingots. The &eDissolver&r gets &b64&r tungsten, &b64&r carbon and &b64&r gold out of it: exactly what went in, atom for atom. A block of nine ingots comes out exact too.
Got it: these have no reverse recipe
Memorize the list of things that don't go back together

These are the mod's own recipes, not the pack's, and the mod wrote them symmetrically. You won't get a printing press out of this: take something apart and put it back together, and you have exactly what you started with. But you haven't lost anything either, and in a world where everything shrinks by half, that counts for a lot.
With an elytra, by the way, Levitation stops being a problem and becomes an elevator.

It has no recipes at all: no crafting, no Combiner, no Dissolver. You can't make it, take it apart or duplicate it. This pack's chemistry has reached almost everything, but the elytra is the one thing in the End it couldn't reach from either side.
There are plenty of one-way ones too, and almost all of them are from around here.

Here and only here you'll find blazes and wither skeletons, and the chests hold things that can't be crafted: saddles, nether wart, flint and steel, horse armor. There aren't many chests, but there are plenty of fortresses: they generate in strips, so once you've found one, look for the next in a straight line.
That's not a floor under you
A brute doesn't barter, doesn't care about your gold and isn't distracted by gold blocks. There's no making a deal with him at all: he's the only piglin built like that.
Nether wart lies in fortress chests and grows in patches under the staircases; there's none anywhere else in the whole game.
It's the only way in the game to die from a fall after starting on the ground and never climbing anything. There's an advancement for exactly this, and getting it is easier than not getting it.
Ash, pillars and a floor that drops you into lava when you step on it. The only living things are ghasts and magma cubes, but there are plenty of them.
Don't break things in front of them

Gilded blackstone is different. Nine groups, and each one is rolled on its own, independently of the others: &b29&r%% for silica, &b20&r%% for eight gold, &b15&r%% for aluminum oxide, &b10&r%% for calcium oxide, &b10&r%% for magnesium oxide, and so on down the list. The &eDissolver&r goes through all nine in a row.

In season one, this gold went to the piglins for iridium and barium. In season two it's needed for its own sake: Draconic Cores, gilded blackstone, wires and circuit boards. And iridium and barium are printed in the same place, the Fusion Chamber, right next to the gold.
A dark red box of bridges and corridors, usually hanging right over a sea of lava.

The spot is the Nether's bedrock ceiling. Dig your way up, carve out a nook, build him there. He can't break &eBedrock&r even with the blue skulls, he has no room to maneuver, and anything else you build he'll wreck.
Return to the Nether, and not for the star this time
&b32&r mendelevium and &b8&r hydroxylapatite, and the skull is assembled. Exactly what it breaks down into.
The floor gives way

Blackstone and basalt dissolve on the same table: &b49&r%% silica, &b15&r%% aluminum oxide, &b10&r%% each for calcium oxide and magnesium oxide, &b7&r%% iron oxide, then small stuff. That's the same magnesium oxide you pay for every new portal: eight per block of obsidian.

A funny pair: one is the most down-to-earth of the rare metals and for that very reason the evidence of a cosmic impact; the other doesn't exist in nature at all and was made atom by atom in an accelerator. And here you get both with a pickaxe and a sword.
Thirty-two is statistics, not a target: skulls drop rarely, and three skulls will take noticeably more kills than that.
So building with purpur costs nothing: take it apart and you get the same lutetium back, plus the silica on top. In a world where everything else loses something in processing, that's a rare treat.
Underfoot is crimson nylium, and it's more generous than stone too: &b10&r%% germanium instead of &b3.7&r%%. It only comes off with Silk Touch; otherwise it crumbles into plain netherrack.
Blazes fly, so falling doesn't kill them and height doesn't help. Forget that too.
Polonium is a ghast

Now look around. For four chapters straight you stood on the same white slab: no horizon, no sound, not a single living thing. Here there's a ceiling, cliffs, lavafalls, five biomes with different weather, and all of it moves and screams.

Four popped fruits give four purpur blocks: not one, four. You keep all the lutetium: it was a half chance per fruit, now it's a half chance per block. And instead of four cellulose, you now get sixteen silica out of them.
Got it: no bartering
A blaze drops zero to one rod; Looting III raises the cap to four. That's the difference between an evening and a week.

Mendelevium is named after the man who came up with the periodic table. It was synthesized one atom at a time: the first experiment produced seventeen atoms in total, and they were counted one by one, by the clicks of a counter.
Chorus grows on its own, right on End Stone, and grows back. Hit the bottom block and the whole plant comes down.
In a world with no grass, no dirt and not a single biome where anything grows, this is the only flower that can appear on its own. Not planted, not printed, but actually grown.
This also works for slabs and pillars, but not for quartz, and that's a separate conversation.
Make 4 Netherite Ingots
Eight creams make eight three-minute potions. Enough for one good run down to the lava and one back.
In real life thulium is the rarest of the lanthanides; there's less of it on the planet than silver. Here it lies around as an entire valley, and things walk on it.

From here on, skulls stop being loot and become a consumable. You can summon the Wither as often as you like, or never at all: the star is printed from &b64&r mendelevium, &b64&r titanium, &b64&r lutetium and &b64&r dysprosium.
Collect 32 Gilded Blackstone
A strider walks on lava and gives you a ride, and the lava lakes here are wider than any bridge you'll ever build.
Thirty-two shells are &b256&r lutetium, four stars. Or sixteen shulker boxes, which will most likely turn out to be more useful.
&7There's no need to make the piglin angry. He'll take your gold and give you nothing in return.&r
An empty bottle into the purple cloud, and you've got Dragon's Breath.

In season one, bartering was a machine that turned gold into half the Nether: crying obsidian with its iridium, quartz with its barium, soul sand with its thulium, pearls and fire resistance. Now each of those goes through chemistry. The Fusion Chamber prints iridium and barium, pearls drop from endermen or get assembled in the &eCombiner&r, and crying obsidian is made on the &6Avaritia&r Sculk Crafting Table.

Here the &eDissolver&r works less like a chemistry instrument and more like a geological one. One block of netherrack is one roll on a seven-row table, and more than half the rolls come up empty: &b55&r%% nothing, &b15&r%% silicon, &b11&r%% sulfur, &b7&r%% zinc oxide, and &b3.7&r%% each for gold, phosphorus and germanium.
A Fission Core is six yttrium ingots and three blaze rods. A chamber needs three cores. Nine rods per chamber, and no chemistry can replace them: there's no Combiner recipe for the rod.

Inside are chests with diamond and iron gear and enchanted books, but most importantly shulkers and the ship. An elytra hangs in an item frame on the ship, and it's the only place in the game where you'll ever find one.
An End Crystal is seven glass, an Eye of Ender and a ghast tear. Four crystals around the edges of the exit portal, and the dragon rises again.
Three cobblestone and a blaze rod.

The setup: a nylium block, a fungus on top, bone meal on the fungus. A huge fungus grows, with shroomlights in its cap and wart blocks as a bonus. Take the nylium with Silk Touch right there in the forest; you print the bone meal; the fungus multiplies on its own from the same bone meal.
Find an End City
Think of it this way: the furnace costs coal, and your coal is six carbon. One and a half percent more germanium for six carbon is a bargain.
You can soften the blow. Fire Resistance potions turn up in bastion chests. But you still have to get to a bastion.
&6You've been here once before, for the star.&r In, grab it, out, and that was the right call.

In real life iridium is rare too, but it's famous for something else. All over the planet, on every continent, the boundary where the Cretaceous ends is marked by a thin layer of clay full of iridium, a hundred times more than the Earth's crust is supposed to hold. The Earth had nowhere inside itself to get that much from. That's how they worked out the asteroid.
Summon and kill the Wither
Eight iridium per block, plus magnesium oxide, potassium chloride, aluminum oxide, silica and phosphorus, all at once and guaranteed.
Two hundred and fifty-six blocks is roughly one and a half thorium. Dig more.
Two lines chemistry never caught up with

Powder goes back together exactly: the same &b8&r, &b8&r and &b2&r. A rod won't: neither the mod nor the pack has a recipe for it. Powder is printed, rods are farmed, and the whole difference between them is one craft that only works in one direction.
Six crying obsidian and three glowstone blocks.
That's by design. You've learned to make any element out of any other, but the machines that do it multiply only through a place where there's something under your feet.
Mercury and neodymium are hard to come by anywhere else: End Stone gives one atom at fourteen and one and a half percent, warped wart four per block. A pearl is sixteen and sixteen at once.
The cheapest trick in the whole chapter, and almost nobody notices it.

Any blocks from the list work for the pyramid: iron, gold, emerald, diamond, netherite. Your iron comes from the rock, eighteen percent per block. So the pyramid costs you not money but Dissolver time.

Netherrack dissolves on a table with a total weight of &b27&r, and &b15&r of that is the empty group. Smelt it in a furnace. A Nether brick dissolves on the same table, but the total is &b18&r, and only &b5&r of it is empty. All seven rows get exactly one and a half times better at once: germanium from &b3.7&r%% to &b5.6&r%%, silicon from &b15&r%% to &b22&r%%, sulfur from &b11&r%% to &b22&r%%.
Stockpile 16 gold blocks
Craft a Brewing Stand
And the math comes out exact: nine nether warts give the same &b36&r germanium as the block made from those nine. Packing loses nothing here, which is rare: usually it's the other way around.
Kill 4 piglin brutes
A Warped Fungus on a Stick is the steering wheel. The fungus grows only in the Warped Forest; the fishing rod is three sticks and two string, and you print string from keratin.
A shulker bullet lifts you about fifty blocks up.
Stand in the Nether Wastes
Your gold comes from the white rock, one percent per block, and an ingot is sixteen atoms. Four ingots for a pair of boots: practically free.
Purpur costs nothing
Even, with no shrinkage
Saddles can't be crafted

In practice: a ghast fires from sixty-four blocks away and hits both your portal and you, and its fireball can be knocked back with anything, fists included. Tears don't always drop, so shoot back with a bow and don't be lazy about picking them up.
Collect 32 Shulker Shells
Kill the Ender Dragon

Radon is the only radioactive gas that occurs on its own, right in the ground. It seeps out of rock into basements and mines, and it's second only to tobacco as a cause of lung cancer. It has no smell and doesn't glow, which is why it's measured with instruments, not noses.
A shell is &b8&r calcium carbonate and &b8&r lutetium. And exactly the same on the way back.
Netherite is packaging
All the thulium in the world
In the previous chapter you were told: if you find a spawner, don't break it. That wasn't the whole truth.
From here on, two things depend on this fortress, and without them reactors don't multiply and potions don't get brewed.
While you're here, grab extra: nether wart grows only on soul sand, and without it there's no brewing.
Make a Warped Fungus on a Stick
Haste at level four
Oganesson is the loudest thing in the breath, but xenon and radon came along too, eight of each per bottle.
Number 118 from a bottle
Grow and harvest 32 Shroomlight
There are five biomes in total, and they aren't scenery: each has its own table and its own elements. Check them all, and then you'll know where to go for what.
Then the dragon itself. When it lands in the middle, hit the head; when it flies, shoot; when it breathes purple, step back and don't get greedy.

The saddle, though, can't be crafted in vanilla or here, and no mod in the pack has a recipe for it. It only turns up in chests: about one chest in seven in a fortress, more often in a bastion. So you'll make the steering wheel at home and start riding once you find your first chest with a saddle.
What's left is an honest room: the spawner, a platform around it, a one-block gap underneath, and you standing below it swinging a sword. Slow, but it works.
So iridium, thorium, oganesson, xenon and radon enter this world exactly once for every block you gather. There's nowhere else to get them, and no way to put them back.
Nine per chamber, just different ones
Read why piglins don't trade anymore
Read this before you pack your bag
You'll have to kill them by hand

In real life, barium is what they give you to drink before an X-ray. The metal itself is poisonous, but barium sulfate doesn't dissolve in anything at all, so it never gets through the intestinal wall and just rides straight through. It does block X-rays, though, so the image shows things that are normally invisible. The one case where people drink poison by the glass and nothing happens, because what matters isn't the formula, it's the solubility.
A trap that costs you a quarter of all the quartz you bring back.

Lutetium goes into the star, &b64&r per print. So it's a hundred and twenty-eight fruit per star, and chorus is endless and guarded by no one. A shulker shell, for comparison, gives eight lutetium at once, but shulkers shoot.
The stand you can't print
Stockpile 512 barium

Meanwhile, everything made from the block dissolves evenly. Bricks: four blocks give four bricks, &b64&r barium each, and it adds up. Pillar: two blocks, two pillars, adds up. Slab, chiseled block, smooth quartz: same. They miscounted exactly one item, and it's the one you make first.

Blue is worth more here: neodymium makes the best magnets on the planet, and you already get germanium from every other block. The only hostiles here are endermen, and they leave you alone as long as you don't look them in the eye. The calmest biome in the Nether.
Collect 64 Chorus Fruit
Make 64 Blaze Powder
Every bridge in this pack gives back half: assemble an ingot from sixteen atoms, take it apart, and you get eight. The rule is strict, and there are no exceptions.
Piglins don't trade anymore
Reach the Crimson Forest and bring back 16 wart blocks
So an enderman here walks around pre-assembled: three elements in a ready-made ratio, and the Combiner turns them into exactly one pearl, while the Dissolver turns it back into exactly those three.
Four hundred blocks for one rod

The egg won't yield to the &eDissolver&r at all: there's no recipe either way. This pack has exactly three such things: the egg, the elytra and the End Crystal. Everything else, in a world where everything comes apart, comes apart.
Fifty blocks up
The skull is a consumable now

A ghast tear is &b16&r polonium. The mod's only other source of polonium is the amethyst geode, and not a single geode grows on the white plain. So polonium in this world means ghasts, and only ghasts.
A red forest of huge fungi, and their caps are built from Nether Wart Blocks.
Once you have the Fusion Chamber, gold gets printed: copper plus tin, &b29&r plus &b50&r, and there's your &b79&r. The white rock is four percent copper, and after diorite you have mountains of tin.
Half a percent of thorium

This mod's first recipe goes like this: drop ingots on the ground and blow them up. Not a furnace, not a press: dynamite next to a pile of iron. A fifth of the ingots are lost in the process, and there's no way around the loss: the Pressure Chamber compresses the same iron without an explosion, but it's built from compressed iron itself.

The Safety Tube Module vents the excess into the atmosphere a tenth of a bar before the danger line. It saves the machine but throws the air away, so it's paired with a Pressure Gauge Tube Module: that one outputs redstone based on pressure, and the redstone shuts the compressor off.

Sulfur in cured rubber: it went into the polymer's cross-links and can't be extracted. Real life works exactly the same way: vulcanization is irreversible, and that's the whole difference between chewing gum and a tire.

The mod's furnace makes them exactly the same way, one step at a time: tough from ferroboron with lithium, extreme from tough with refractory metals. The bridges repeat this ladder in atoms instead of cutting it short.

The reason is that it doesn't unlock anything: it's iron, redstone and logs, and all three are already bridged separately. A bridge here would be a second path to the same item, meaning one more recipe in every machine's endless loop, and not a single new possibility.
In the Combiner, zirconium and hafnium are two independent lines, and you take them separately without the slightest trouble.

Half is the default rule, not a law. Where a mod can make the same item cheaper, the breakdown has been cut by hand.

An apple in the Combiner is sucrose and cellulose, so there is sugar in this world after all; you can only get to it through apples. One more thing: fermentation is exothermic, so the plant heats itself up, and it's easy to overshoot the window's sixty-degree upper limit and stall.

It's also the second uranium oxide in this chapter. &6Mekanism&r has yellowcake, three uranium atoms per eight oxygen. Here it's the dioxide, one to two. Different stoichiometry of the same element, and both are honest: yellowcake is what leaves the mine, and the dioxide is what later goes into a fuel pellet.

The &6PneumaticCraft&r refinery won't take this oil; it needs its own. It gets upgraded in the Thermopneumatic Processing Plant: a bucket of synthetic oil and one emerald per bucket, at a hundred degrees. The emerald's chromium and beryllium act as a catalyst, like the chromia-alumina catalysts in real cracking. The price is the same as before, an emerald per barrel, just without the drones.
Remember the three exceptions to the reversibility rule.

What matters more is what drops out alongside it. Together with the biodiesel you get a drop of glycerol; at a real plant it's a byproduct there's so much of that nobody knows what to do with it. Here it's exactly what will later unlock speed upgrades, so don't throw it away.
An “elements → uranium-&b235&r” bridge would cost two lines of code and kill an entire mod. That's why it doesn't exist and never will.
It also closes a loophole: latex is renewable, and without this caveat a rubber plantation would become a free source of sulfur.

Kaolinite is clay by &6Alchemistry&r's chemistry, and clay in an insulator is nothing unusual. The strange part is something else: graphite is a conductor, and it seemingly has no place in a dielectric paste.
Cellulose gives a log. The log grows into a tree. The tree gives latex. Latex gives plastic. Plastic gives PVC. PVC gives carbon, hydrogen and chlorine, which is back into chemistry.
In a world where literally everything is reversible, exactly one item goes only one way. It's not optimization and not forgetfulness: it's the one place where the pack says “no” without any caveats.

One bridge carries an entire branch of the mod. And there isn't a gram of fluorine in the rock, so you'll have to synthesize it first.

The interface isn't free: a thousand milliliters of air for each item it moves. A full stack is sixty-four thousand, which is four bar for a small chamber. If the interface has frozen, it isn't broken, it's saving up.

Food in this world is printed from sucrose and cellulose, and the red dye for this compressor comes from beetroot, which is also built in the Combiner. Your first bar of pressure is paid for with the same carbon as everything else, just by the longest route.

The practical problem is something else. Neither lead nor neodymium is in the rock, and thirty-two graphite make enderium the most carbon-hungry bridge in &6Thermal&r. Your first ingot will cost more than the entire branch before it.

Carborundum was discovered by accident while trying to synthesize diamond, and it turned out almost as hard: all of the twentieth century's sandpaper is made from it. Tungsten carbide is three times harder than steel and holds up to heat, so it's used to cut steel itself.

Not one ore, not a drop of oil from the ground, not a single item that was just lying around in the world. Mushroom, apple and seed were built in the Combiner, they gave ethanol and oil, those gave biodiesel, biodiesel gave plastic, the plastic went into a tablet, and the tablet bought what can't be crafted at all.

Two of this mod's items used to be purchase-only, and both are now crafted at a workbench from emeralds for the same price. The PCB Blueprint from eight emeralds and paper, the Assembly Line programs from an emerald block, paper and a marker ingredient. Chemistry can do a great deal; some things you have to pay for in emeralds.

The Empty PCB is pressed in the chamber from wiring and redstone torches. Then it's exposed to UV through the blueprint for ten minutes, and then etched with acid. An underexposed board risks coming out of the etch as a dud, and a dud is smelted in a blast furnace back into an empty one: the loop is closed, but it eats time.

Ruby and sapphire are the same mineral, corundum. Chromium makes it red; iron with titanium makes it blue. Great chemistry, the bridge practically suggested itself.
&6NuclearCraft&r winds coils from it. The mod seems to have read the same news.

Everything that works here has a volume in milliliters and air pumped inside it. Pressure is derived from those: divide the air by the volume and subtract one. A volume of five thousand with twenty thousand air gives three bar.

The build order doesn't matter, but the cube won't form at all if even one block on an edge is wrong. And you can't spot the mistake by eye: a wall and a valve look alike. Check the edges, not the faces.

&6Mekanism&r counts energy, &6Alchemistry&r counts atoms, and this one counts milliliters of air and degrees. Three different sets of books on one raw material, and all three balance in the Dissolver.

Eight emeralds for a piece of exposed film. Without it you can't build the UV Light Box, without the box you can't expose the board, without exposure you can't etch it. The other path to the board goes through the Assembly Line, and the line's programs are made from an emerald block.
Two parts nothing works without

Both are superconductors, and both are working right now in hardware you could touch. NbTi is wound into every MRI magnet and most of the Large Hadron Collider's magnets. Nb₃Sn holds a field twice as strong and so goes into tokamaks, but it's as brittle as glass, so the coil is wound first and annealed afterwards, letting the compound form right inside the finished winding.

The culture has a second way to multiply: pour it into a puddle, toss in sugar, add water next to it. Sugar doesn't exist in this world at all: no sugar cane, no bees, and the Combiner doesn't make it. So that leaves only the plant, and this recipe runs ten times slower on it than any other. Build a second plant right away; you'll thank yourself later.

These are all salts for the molten salt reactor: the fluorides are the melt itself, and borax opens up the decay branch. NaF and KF even have minerals of their own, villiaumite and carobbiite, both so rare that it's easier to make them in the Combiner.

Four calcium and eight fluorine. CaF₂, fluorite, the mineral that gave a phenomenon its name: fluorescence is named after it, not the other way around.

And here a bridge won't help. A piece of a mob cage has no chemical meaning: it's not a substance, it's a structural part. Inventing a composition for it would be the same kind of lie as a bridge to uranium-&b235&r.

So any ingot from any mod is sixteen atoms, split according to the alloy's real composition. Bronze: fourteen copper and two tin. Stainless steel: twelve iron, three chromium, one nickel. Zircaloy: fourteen zirconium, one tin, one iron. The total is always the same.

The bridges for alloys, circuits and servos, however, use strontium carbonate: those recipes were written from &6Alchemistry&r's own breakdown, where the red color comes from strontium. And that's honest: strontium burns red, calcium gives orange.

Brewing something once in a corner of your base and putting it on a production line are two different kinds of engineering. The first takes knowing chemistry. The second takes knowing logistics, because by then chemistry stopped being the problem long ago.

A pleasant breather in the middle of a list where half the components only show up after chapter six.

This is the most direct bridge in the pack, and also the most generous: the rock gives twelve percent silicon, third place after iron and carbon. All the electronics on the planet are made from this element, and yours are too.

The line between “it worked” and “it works without me” runs right here.
An &6Alchemistry&r machine goes through the entire recipe list of its type every tick. Not at load time: every tick, and every machine separately.
And the physics is real: polonium-&b210&r really is made by irradiating bismuth in a reactor, not dug up. This is usually the spot where you feel like yelling something about science.

Manganese does two things in steel at once: it binds the sulfur that makes hot metal crack, and it improves hardenability. The first one matters more: before manganese, steel tore apart in the rolling mill and nobody understood why.

Twenty Dissolvers on one pipe form a queue. Twenty Dissolvers on twenty pipes tank the tick rate. XNet does its work in a single block for the whole network, so a line on XNet is cheaper than a line on pipes, and an &6AE2&r Pattern Provider is cheaper than both, except it only handles exactly two machines: the Combiner and the Compactor.

The second one lives: instead of sugar, a drop of glycerol, that very waste from biodiesel, and the output is two upgrades instead of one. The mod meant this as a reward for those who made it to renewable fuel. For us it's simply the only way, and it's twice as good to boot.

This is the most valuable return path in the whole pack, the only bridge that was written right to left. A &6Mekanism&r reactor breeds polonium and plutonium from fission waste. The &eDissolver&r turns a pellet into atoms, and the atoms go into the Combiner for whatever else you want. These two elements have no other source in the pack.

Han purple is a real substance, BaCuSi₂O₆, a synthetic pigment from Bronze Age China. It was made two thousand years ago, the recipe was lost, and its composition was only worked out in the twentieth century from the paint on the Terracotta Warriors. And at low temperatures it even loses a dimension: excitations in it stop propagating along the third axis.

Here purity isn't a number, it's an item type. An iron atom is either iron, or it's already a different item. You can't dilute something and pass it off as pure: the game counts atoms, not percent, and the Combiner won't take fifteen instead of sixteen.

In &6Thermal&r and &6Mekanism&r, resources can at least in theory be mined as ore. Here the way into the mod is world generation, all of it: darkstone in layers, arcane crystal ore, runic stone, meteorites, edelwood trees in swamps. None of that exists in a flat world.

Break down any of these items and you get atoms. Build another mod's item from those same atoms, and it adds up. A &6Mekanism&r reactor breeds polonium, the Dissolver turns it into elements, and the elements go into a &6NuclearCraft&r superconductor or a &6Powah&r crystal. Tin, lead, silver, nickel. In the code these are four identical lines: sixteen atoms per ingot, eight back. No composition, no backstory.
Redstone dust in this world is made from iron oxide and calcium carbonate. It had to be: the first machine needed to be built before anything more exotic showed up.

Refined Glowstone: sixteen phosphorus and four osmium in, and only four phosphorus back, not a single atom of osmium. Because the Osmium Compressor makes this ingot from one pinch of glowstone dust, and a pinch is four phosphorus. Let the bridge return eight and two, and you'd have a double pump on two elements at once.

These formulas aren't made up. They're the mod's own recipes, converted into atoms through &6Alchemistry&r breakdowns: blaze powder gives germanium and sulfur, phantom membrane gives cerium, gunpowder gives niter, bone meal gives hydroxyapatite, and an ender pearl gives silicon, mercury and neodymium.

Everything else follows from this formula. A machine consumes air, not pressure; the pressure just drops as a result. A volume upgrade doesn't add power: it makes the pressure dip shallower. And zero bar isn't a vacuum, it's normal atmosphere: vacuum starts at minus one.
The whole nickel branch of &6Thermal&r (invar, constantan, and half of &6NuclearCraft&r's stainless steel) runs into nickel, not iron. Give it a Dissolver of its own, and more than one.

Of the others, you can forget about the electrostatic one here: it feeds on lightning, and the biome has no precipitation, so there will be neither rain nor thunderstorms. Formally there's still a chance of a strike in clear weather, but it's so small that a lifetime isn't enough. The thermal one wants a temperature difference across opposite faces, and the liquid one wants fuel you don't have yet.

The breakdown returns only gold. The mod's recipe has no molybdenum or cobalt, and the pack has no other source of them either: if the bridge returned them, deorum would become a generator of two elements out of nothing. The same trick as with sulfur in rubber: the alloying addition went into the alloy and can't be extracted.

So a bridge isn't a one-time cost, it's a permanent tax on every machine of that type on the map. That's why the alloy list was trimmed, and fission and fusion weren't touched at all: fusion has three and a half thousand recipes, and nothing may be added there under any circumstances.
Small amounts come back whole: if an alloy contains just one unit of some alloying element, half of it is still one. You won't get rich on carbon and manganese.

Every tech mod in this pack has the same problem: each one starts with ore. Tin, osmium, uranium, arcane, it doesn't matter. &cThere is not a single ore&r, world generation is switched off entirely, and played straight, not one of them would ever open up at all.

For organics the window is narrow: thirty to sixty degrees. Below that it doesn't run, above that it doesn't either. A Thermostat Module on a tube can measure the temperature of the neighboring block and output redstone, and building one once is easier than chasing the window by hand.

Ferroboron has its own place in a reactor: boron swallows neutrons, iron holds the shape. And in the rest of the world, the same composition with added neodymium makes the strongest permanent magnets humanity knows how to produce.

Thorium's story is a sad one: there's three times more of it in the Earth's crust than uranium, reactors run on it without piling up long-lived waste, but industry went down the uranium path, largely because uranium also gave weapons-grade plutonium. &6NuclearCraft&r dutifully offers both branches, and here nobody has taken the choice away from you.
Exactly two units of redstone, and one comes back. Half of two. On strontium the round trip comes out at exactly zero, and that's not greed, it's the only way to avoid opening a pump.

In reality this is one of the most agonizing problems in all of metallurgy. Zirconium and hafnium are chemically almost indistinguishable, occur in the same ore and are separated through dozens of extraction stages. And separating them is a must: zirconium is transparent to neutrons, while hafnium swallows them six hundred times more greedily. Fuel rod cladding made of unpurified zirconium simply won't let the reactor start.
Same check as everywhere: the mod's Enrichment Chamber makes two of these from a uranium ingot, which is sixteen atoms. Breaking down two gives six. The direct route is better.

The phosphorus isn't there for weight: &6Alchemistry&r breaks glowstone dust down into pure phosphorus, and that's no poetic license. White phosphorus really does glow in the dark on its own, which is how it got its name: “light-bearer”.

A liter of water and a handful of mushrooms at thirty to sixty degrees give a quarter liter of yeast culture. All of the mod's organics start here, and neither ingredient exists in this world: water is combined from hydrogen and oxygen, the mushroom from phosphoric acid and chitin.

The practical takeaway: you'll need strontium not for the dust itself but for everything built from it. The rock holds six tenths of a percent, the tail end of a list of twenty-five elements. Plan your Dissolver ahead.

The bridge isn't about the planks. All four Hephaestus Forge upgrade rituals depend on edelwood planks, and edelwood has no sapling: it only grows in swamps, which don't exist here. Without these six cellulose the forge stays at tier one forever.
And &eantimatter&r. There is no Dissolver recipe for it, period. The only item in the game that goes one way only.

Natural uranium is bridged. Uranium-&b235&r, uranium-&b238&r, plutonium-&b239&r, thorium-&b232&r and all the rest are not, and this is the most principled refusal in the whole chapter.
For thousands of years cinnabar was two things at once: mercury ore and red paint. Painters ground it into vermilion, metallurgists heated it to get mercury, and both trades ended the same way.
Every upgrade in the mod has four lapis lazuli in the corners. Lapis here is synthetic (silicon, sodium, mullite and calcium sulfide), and it's hard to call it cheap.
Neither is in the rock. Both will come from fusion, and both at sixteen atoms per ingot, like everything else.

The mod makes it from manganese steel and titanium, and this is the chapter's second asymmetry. Trading “titanium for silicon and carbon” doesn't pay off for the player, so the real composition stayed.

The lamp will take any fuel, but kerosene is the most efficient in it, LPG included. The only spot in the mod where a middle fraction beats a light one, and a good reason not to burn kerosene in a compressor.

The Vortex Tube is a real device, not a game convention. Compressed air swirls inside and exits from both ends: hot from one, cold from the other. Not a single moving part, just the geometry of the vortex.

A deep loss on carbon, and rightly so. The rock is fourteen percent carbon, and carbon is truly renewable through trees; if you're going to cycle it, alloys are definitely not the way.

A neutron loses energy better the closer the mass of whatever it hits is to its own. Think billiards: a heavy ball barely slows a neutron down, a light one stops it beautifully. Hence the whole list of moderators: hydrogen, carbon, beryllium.
Eight ethylene per pellet. Nothing needed translating: HDPE is high-density polyethylene, and ethylene is exactly its monomer. Polymerization as it is.

This is microalloying, and the numbers in the bridge are no exaggeration: real steel of this class needs hundredths of a percent of niobium. It precipitates as tiny carbides and keeps the grain from growing: strength goes up by a third from an amount you'd weigh on pharmacy scales.
There's nothing to drive out here; graphite is already pure carbon. So our bridge is more honest than the real process: there's no stage where anything gets lost.

Osmium is the densest of the stable elements: a cubic meter weighs twenty-two and a half tonnes. But for the pack something else matters more. Actually it does. In real high-voltage cables the insulation is coated on both sides with a semiconducting layer based on carbon black: it evens out the electric field and keeps it from tearing the insulation apart at microscopic bumps. A dielectric with carbon inside isn't a mistake in the mod; it's exactly how a cable is built.

SiC/SiC composite is silicon carbide fiber in a silicon carbide matrix: the same substance in two roles. Ceramic on its own is brittle, but fiber in a matrix catches a crack and doesn't let it run all the way through. Next-generation fuel cladding is made from composites like this: unlike zircaloy, they don't release hydrogen when they overheat.

The &eCertificate&r asks for the prediction itself, not the matrix. A matrix is a blank, you craft it on your first evening. A prediction is proof that the farm has been running for a long time.
Hold 64 predictions

The fabricator breaks a filled Prediction down into the exact drops a living mob would give: bones, gunpowder, arrows, ender pearls, skulls. It doesn't print metals, gems or coal: in this pack raw materials come only from chemistry.
24 · Hostile Networks
It eats power and nothing else: no water, no spawning, no platform. It works in a closed box at your base.
Generalized Predictions aren't the loot of one specific mob but the distilled essence of a whole dimension. They only come from a model brought up to the top tier.
And you need them all the time: spirits for &6Malum&r, materials for &6Apotheosis&r, gunpowder, bones, slime, wither skeleton skulls for Nether Stars.
Four regular Predictions are crafted into one Generalized Prediction.
Craft it and record your first model
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.25_cryo_acc: The frame is the same as the Fission and Fusion Chambers: a &b5×5×5&r cube. The &6Alchemistry&r book has a ready 3D plan in the reactor section, page "Cryo Chamber Multiblock". Its &eVisualize&r button highlights every missing block right in the world.
&aTwo of these crystals go into every Infinity Catalyst.&r The finale needs thousands of catalysts, so one chamber is only the beginning, not the end.
Without the Cryo Chamber there are no magnets at all. That's the whole point: the accelerator doesn't stand off to the side of the chemistry, it grows out of it.
Make 2 NbTi Alloy ingots
Get a Dark Matter Cell
The formula reads straight off: one yttrium, two barium, three copper, seven oxygen. Four elements for exactly four &eCombiner&r slots, and nobody fudged it: that's simply how the ceramic is made.
25 · Cold and the Accelerator
Four kelvins
&7The blend only dissolves back into half of what went in, and without the yttrium: it is the most expensive of the four, and the Dissolver is not going to become a way to squeeze it out.&r
Get 4 YBCO Superconductors
Yttrium and barium don't occur in the rock; chapter six's fusion makes them. Copper and oxygen are your own, from the rock.
YBa₂Cu₃O₇
On its own the alloy is nothing special: strong, heat-resistant, gray. Only the cold makes it remarkable.
Make 4 YBCO Blend
Two small cells go into every &6Draconic Evolution&r Chaotic Core.
Build a Particle Injector and 8 Electromagnetic Boosters
Make three Cryo Cores
&7The ring draws power from an &6Electrodynamics&r grid, and that grid has voltage. Get it wrong and the machine can blow up, so put transformers before it, not after.&r
Dark matter
Got it

Superconductors are needed by two things: the &6Nuclear Science&r accelerator, without which that mod has no antimatter and no dark matter, and every &eInfinity Catalyst&r in the finale. Two per catalyst.
Minus a hundred and ninety-six
Three of these cables go into the &6Draconic Evolution&r Reactor Core: its field is held by magnets too.
Build 16 Electromagnets
Niobium and titanium
Get 8 NbTi cables
Motor, plates, cable

Where things go. The cores stack in the very center, layers two to four. The controller goes in the middle of a wall, second row from the bottom. The ports go on any of the &b12&r edges of the cube, not in the middle of a wall. Top and bottom are solid casing, the wall centers are casing or glass. Everything else inside stays empty.
The accelerator is a ring of electromagnets around which the &eParticle Injector&r drives particles. Magnets, boosters and Electromagnetic Glass all go into the ring.
Two more sit in every &6Draconic Evolution&r Energy Core. Superconducting energy storage is meant literally there: current runs around the cold ring without loss.
The peak of &6Nuclear Science&r and a line on the &eCertificate&r transcript.
The Large Hadron Collider runs its &b1232&r main magnets on exactly this kind of cable, cooled with helium almost to absolute zero. The scale here is more modest, the principle is the same.
An alloy ingot and &b8&r helium give two cables. NbTi only superconducts below &b10&r K, which nitrogen can't reach, so it takes helium, and helium comes from fusion: hydrogen plus hydrogen.
All the chemistry so far has climbed up the temperature scale: the Dissolver, reactors, smelteries. This chapter goes the other way.
The chamber eats a lot of power: &b800&r FE/t, &b20&r seconds per operation. Build it with plenty of spare power from the start.

For exactly how to build the ring and what to feed the injector, check &eJEI&r and the mod itself: &6Nuclear Science&r has its own logic, and retelling it from memory is a sure way to get something wrong.
Read

Antimatter that wasn't assembled from shards on a crafting table but made in an accelerator, the way it's made for real. Half a gram is monstrously much by the standards of physics: real accelerators have produced nanograms in their entire history.
&8Twelve grams of antimatter meeting matter would release the energy of a nuclear explosion. Good thing this is Minecraft.&r

There is five times more dark matter in the Universe than ordinary matter, and nobody really knows what it is. It shows up only through gravity: galaxies rotate as if they held mass that nobody can see.
Eight atoms each of niobium and titanium, sixteen per ingot: the pack's scale. Niobium comes from fusion, titanium from the rock or the Enricher's Trace Concentrate.

You need: the controller, &b3&r Cryo Cores, one each of Reactor Energy Input, Reactor Item Input and Reactor Item Output, &b59&r Reactor Casing and &b35&r Reactor Glass. Glass can be swapped for casing, then it is &b94&r casing.

In real life YBCO was discovered in &b1987&r, and it was a revolution: for the first time a superconductor worked not in expensive helium but in cheap nitrogen. The Nobel Prize for high-temperature superconductivity was awarded that same year, to Bednorz and Müller, who had discovered the first such ceramic a year earlier. It hardly ever gets faster than that.

The &eCryo Chamber&r is the first multiblock that exists in no mod at all: it was built here, for this server. The frame is a familiar one, like the fission and fusion reactors, with three &eCryo Cores&r inside.
The pack now has three antimatters: the white one the world is made of, &6Mekanism&r pellets and &6Nuclear Science&r cells. Each has its own road, and all three meet in the finale.
Twelve grams
Build the whole chamber and start it up
Seventy-seven kelvins
The cores stack into a three-block column in the center of the future chamber. While the chamber is idle they stay dark, and they light up as soon as it starts working.
Cryo Chamber
Get a small Anti-Matter Cell
Dark matter is what the &eCertificate&r asks for: the accelerator gives antimatter earlier and more easily, while dark matter proves the ring has been pushed all the way.

Cryo Core: the column inside the chamber, like the core of the reactors. Reactor Glass, titanium and nitrogen: the glass keeps the cold in sight, the titanium holds the structure together, and the nitrogen is what it's all for.

Liquid nitrogen boils at &b−196&r °C. That is cold enough for &eYBCO&r ceramic to lose all resistance: current flows through it without loss, forever. Liquid helium is colder still, and in it an alloy of niobium and titanium becomes a superconductor, the very alloy the Large Hadron Collider's magnets are wound from.

In this pack, &6Nuclear Science&r Electromagnets are wound with superconductor: two NbTi cables on either side of a motor. There are two recipes: the cheap one with steel and bronze gives one magnet, the expensive one with HSLA steel and titanium gives fifteen at once.
The ring
The blend and &b8&r nitrogen go into the Cryo Chamber, slot order doesn't matter: the machine works out what goes where by itself. The nitrogen boils away, so it is consumed, not a catalyst.
Optional. Simply the biggest antimatter cell the mod has.
If any port is missing or the frame has a mistake, the controller stays gray and its window won't open. That isn't a bug, it's a sign the structure didn't form.

In the mod, the accelerator makes it when two particles collide at almost top speed. A little slower and you get antimatter instead, and not from every collision at that. Each product takes one empty Electromagnetic Cell.
A cold heart
Five hundred milligrams
The big antimatter cell
Chamber built and running
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.26_factory_: &8Bitumen is thousands of years older than the oil industry: natural bitumen held together the Processional Way back in Babylon.&r
26 · The Factory Must Grow
The blast furnace breathes hot air. It's heated by &eBlast Stoves&r, also called Cowper stoves: fireproof towers named after the engineer Edward Cowper, who patented them in &b1857&r.
Volts and ohms
&7Furnace gas can fuel those same Cowper stoves. A closed loop, just like at a real steel mill.&r
Diesel
The &eEngine Controller&r is a line of the &eCertificate&r transcript. Whoever has built it has gone through the whole factory, from the coke oven to etching boards.
Some recipes need heat: a blaze burner or a TFMG firebox under the vat.
Controller, 6 outputs and pipes
Make 16 Heavy Machinery Casings
The light stuff gathers at the top, the heavy stuff at the bottom, exactly as in a real tower.
&ePonder&r shows how to build any machine in the mod: hover over an item and hold &eW&r.

Without &ereinforcements&r the furnace won't work, and the more of them around it, the faster it runs. Everything is loaded through the opening on top. A second hatch on that opening collects furnace gas, and items sent into it fall into the furnace.
TFMG electricity follows Ohm's law. A generator provides voltage and power, every device has its own resistance, and current equals voltage divided by resistance. A light bulb is &b100&r ohms.
Molten steel from the blast furnace goes into a &eCasting Basin&r and sets into ingots. The basin holds very little: take the ingots out right away, or the whole melt grinds to a halt.
The ingot is the same one &6Mekanism&r makes: there's only one steel in the pack. The difference is scale: the blast furnace melts iron in a stream, not one ingot at a time.
Furnace output, two hatches and 8 reinforcements
Cowper stove
&7There are no pumpjacks or surface scanners in the pack: there isn't a single deposit in the world, and there's no point building a monument that pumps nothing.&r

Three plastic sheets and green dye make an empty board. A &eDeployer&r lays a gold sheet on it. The vat etches it with sulfuric acid, and the traces are left behind. Then an assembly line: a capacitor, two resistors, a transistor.

Sand, cement and gravel in a mixer give concrete mixture, and the mixture with water gives liquid concrete. The liquid is poured into a form and sets into blocks. With slag instead of sand you get twice as much mixture.
Grind 32 limesand
Vulcanization
Cast 12 plastic sheets
&aDon't dump the creosote.&r It fuels the blast furnace's Cowper stoves, and planks soaked in it go into steel casing. It drips out at one mB per piece of coal, so you can never have too many ovens.

The tower's base: steel tanks. Next to them goes the &econtroller&r, above them up to six &eoutputs&r, with industrial pipes in between. The tanks need a heat source underneath, and the gauge on the tower shows whether there's enough. Oil is poured into the controller.
Circuit board
Six fractions
Place a casting basin and cast steel
Devices in one group share the voltage between them; in different groups, each one gets all of it. A transformer changes the voltage by the ratio of turns in its coils, just like a real one.
Black gold
A bucket of each
Fireproof bricks are made from fireclay, clay that withstands the heat of a blast furnace. In TFMG, fireclay lies in veins underground. Here, underground is antimatter.
&7It won't be cheap: hydrogen drops out of the rock in eight rolls out of a hundred, and one crude takes about two hundred dissolved blocks.&r
Coke: coal with everything volatile driven out of it by heat. What's left is almost pure carbon: it burns hotter and doesn't cake in the blast furnace.
&7Don't throw the slag away. The basin casts it into blocks, a crusher grinds them, and slag goes into concrete and asphalt instead of sand, doubling the mix you get.&r

There's no oil in this world, and nowhere to pump it from. So it's made the way Germany made it during the war and South Africa made it under embargo: carbon monoxide and hydrogen are stitched into hydrocarbon chains on a catalyst, and the oxygen leaves as water. Fischer-Tropsch synthesis, &b1925&r.
Air is pumped in by an &eAir Intake&r: a propeller on a shaft.
Distillation tower

Diesel and kerosene go into engines. LPG, butane and propane burn in the firebox, which heats machines like a blaze burner. Naphtha will become plastic, heavy oil will become rubber and bitumen for asphalt.
Fill 2 buckets of oil
A steel vat, a mixer and a blade
Cast iron
The sand also goes into cement: mixed with clay in a mixer. Cement then becomes concrete.
Got it
Cast iron: iron with more than two percent carbon in it. Brittle, but it pours and holds heat, so TFMG makes its pipes, tanks and half its furnaces out of it.

The whole mod comes together in it. Two boards: plastic, gold, acid and an assembly line. Three rubber sheets: heavy oil from the tower, which means synthetic crude and the Liquifier. A steel mechanism and heavy casing: the blast furnace.

An industrial mixer with a blade makes the vat mix. The same mixer turns it into a centrifuge. Two holders with copper electrodes make the vat an electrolyzer, three graphite electrodes make it an arc furnace for steel.
Make 8 rubber sheets
A large engine, an exhaust and oil
Make 2 circuit boards
Fireclay

&6Create: The Factory Must Grow&r brings heavy industry in the spirit of &6Create&r: coke ovens, a blast furnace, a distillation tower, diesel engines and its own electricity, where current has volts and ohms.
The acid is cooked in a vat: three sulfur dust, a nitrate dust and a bucket of water give half a bucket of acid, and one board takes a quarter. A crusher occasionally knocks nitrate dust out of dirt.
A bucket of heavy oil under a press over heat gives bitumen. Bitumen, sand and gravel give asphalt mixture, and with water it turns into liquid asphalt.
Lay 64 blocks of asphalt
The &eLiquifier&r turns synthetic crude into real liquid oil: one item gives half a bucket.
Heavy oil and sulfur dust in a vat with a mixer, over heat, give a rubber sheet. &b250&r mB of oil per sheet.
Place 8 coke ovens and get 32 coal coke
Pour and break 64 blocks of concrete
From there you can pipe it straight into the tower; buckets are only needed for this quest.

Rubber is vulcanized with sulfur in real life too. Charles Goodyear discovered it in &b1839&r, by the famous story, when he dropped a mix of rubber and sulfur on a hot stove. Without sulfur, rubber gets sticky in summer and cracks in winter.
Craft 16
In the blast furnace the sand works as flux: it binds the waste rock into slag, which drains off separately from the metal. Real blast furnaces use the very same limestone for this.
A generator, a converter and an electric gauge

An engine is built from blocks in a line, up to five in a row. Which parts go into the blocks is spelled out in the engine's own tooltip: cylinders, or blades for a turbine. The shaft goes in with a right-click, and the engine starts on a redstone signal.
Steel mechanism

&aThe second way comes from the pack's chemistry:&r ChemLib ethylene from the &eCombiner&r (&b2&r carbon and &b4&r hydrogen), through the &eLiquifier&r and straight into the vat. A sheet comes out about ten times cheaper than through oil.
It's made in a &6Create&r basin under a mechanical press: an iron ingot and coal. It needs heat: a cold basin won't take the recipe.
One plank takes &b250&r mB of creosote. Now you see why the coke ovens need a whole row.

&7The fuel works for &6PneumaticCraft&r too: its compressors recognize TFMG diesel, kerosene, gasoline and LPG by their shared tags. But its refinery won't take the oil itself directly: first it has to be upgraded in a thermopneumatic processing plant, one emerald per bucket. That's how chapter ten keeps its price.&r
Six outputs, six fractions. From &b340&r mB of oil: &b120&r heavy oil, &b60&r each of diesel, gasoline and LPG, &b30&r kerosene and &b10&r naphtha.
Plastic here is polyethylene, a chain of ethylene molecules. The melt is cooked in a vat with a mixer over heat, and the casting basin casts a sheet from &b200&r mB of melt.
Coke
The engine's brain
Craft the engine controller and a transmission
Read
A fireclay ball is fired in a furnace into a fireproof brick. Four bricks make a block.
In go iron dust or crushed iron, limesand and ground coke. Out come molten steel, slag and furnace gas.
Lubricant is topped up with an &eOil Can&r: right-click the engine with it.
The &eChemical Vat&r: one machine with many roles, and the attachments decide which one it plays.

The &eEngine Controller&r sets the speed and direction of the engines' rotation. It's linked with a transmission: right-click the controller with it, then the engine. The control keys are in Minecraft's controls settings, in the TFMG section.

Ethylene comes two ways. The native way is from naphtha: a vat over heat breaks it down into ethylene and propylene, and both work for plastic. But there's little naphtha in oil, &b10&r mB out of &b340&r.
Make 32 blocks of fireproof bricks
Make 4 Synthetic Crude
The flat world finally gets roads, and not one of them needs a bridge.
Chemical vat
Plastic

The &eConverter&r turns TFMG current into FE and back, so a generator on a shaft can feed Dissolvers too. The &eElectric Gauge&r, a voltmeter, shows what's going on in the network: look at it through engineer's goggles.
Press 32 cast iron ingots
Heavy oil can be distilled again: &b200&r mB gives &b25&r mB of lubrication oil and a little diesel, kerosene and naphtha, and half comes back as heavy oil.

Three blocks stacked on top of each other (or a 3×2 platform) make the smallest stove, and blocks on top give it more capacity. Fuel goes in at the bottom, &ecreosote&r or furnace gas; air goes in at the side of the bottom block, and carbon dioxide is pumped out from there too. Hot air comes out of the top.

A plank soaked in &ecreosote&r under a spout, plus a steel ingot, gives &eSteel Casing&r. Add a steel sheet on top and you get &eHeavy Machinery Casing&r. Both are applied by clicking a block, like &6Create&r casings.
Place 3 blast stoves and an air intake
&b8&r carbon monoxide and &b16&r hydrogen in the &eCombiner&r give one &eSynthetic Crude&r. It's the pack's own item and doesn't exist in any mod.
Fischer and Tropsch

A &6Create&r precision mechanism, only made of steel. The workpiece is a heavy plate. Down the line, &eDeployers&r put in a steel cogwheel, a nickel sheet, a large steel cogwheel, a lead sheet and a screw, and the last pass is done with a screwdriver. Two loops.
The mechanism goes into the tower, the vat's mixer and the engines. You can't take a step further without it.
The Factory Must Grow
A large engine needs air and fuel: diesel, kerosene, naphtha or furnace gas, and the carbon dioxide has to be vented through an &eExhaust&r. Fuel and exhaust connect to any block.
&7Real boards are etched the same way, just with a different acid. The principle is the same: the copper covered by the pattern stays, the rest is eaten away.&r
The blast furnace
Almost no rejects: &b120&r chances out of &b128&r. The rest: a compass or a steel ingot.
In a world that's one flat plane to the horizon, concrete finally lets you build something that looks like a city.
Heavy casing
Two boards go into every &6Draconic Evolution&r reactor stabilizer.

In a normal world all of this rests on ore and on oil from underground. Here there are four layers of antimatter under your feet, so three things are built from atoms: &efireclay&r for fireproof bricks, &elimestone&r for flux and cement, and &eoil&r, which comes from Fischer-Tropsch synthesis.

The oven is slow, a minute per piece of coal, so they're built in long rows. Coal goes in from any side. Carbon dioxide leaves from the top, &ecreosote&r from the other sides, and the coke drops out by itself.
The first cast
Blast furnace, oil, diesel
&6This is what the whole chapter was for.&r
Flux
The road
The blast furnace cast its first ingot
So fireclay is put together in the &eCombiner&r: &b2&r kaolinite and &b1&r alumina. Fireclay really is just kaolin with extra aluminum: the more Al₂O₃, the hotter the furnace it can stand.
Concrete
The heart of the blast furnace: the &eBlast Furnace Output&r. Around it goes a cylinder of fireproof bricks, with one &ehatch&r in the wall: hot air from the Cowper stoves comes in through it.
&eLimestone&r: calcium carbonate, CaCO₃. It's put together in the &eCombiner&r from two carbonates, and &6Create&r crushing wheels grind it into &elimesand&r.
lanminecraft.reforged.quests.27_contract: Contracts are repeatable orders. You hand in a batch of something you can already make and get experience for it. Each contract reopens after twenty hours: log in for the evening, and there's something to deliver again.
&8The client never gave a name. Rumor has it they're from the universe next door.&r
The server's shared goal is in &b/season&r: how much antimatter everyone has gathered together. &b/firsts&r shows who finished each chapter first.
Eight mechanisms take about ten attempts on the line. If your line runs on its own, this contract costs you nothing but gold.
Your Cryo Chamber is already up and running. Four crystals cost eighty seconds of its work and a little yttrium.
&7Contract goods are taken when you hand them in: open the contract and click the task.&r
Every &6AE2&r processor starts with silicon. The neighbors need a network too.
The lab needs concentrate: that's what the rare stuff gets squeezed out of. Sixteen concentrates are two hundred and fifty-six blocks of rock run through the Enricher.
Eight Synthetic Crude carry the hydrogen of one thousand six hundred dissolved blocks. Expensive, which is why it pays more experience.
Everyone needs steel, always. Sixty-four ingots: a day's quota for a small workshop.
The most expensive order: a single cell, for which the accelerator gets pushed all the way to the limit.
